item.title: C. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION.REVISED. PYTHON
item.description: # RP9_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED.py # Version: 2.0.0 # Purpose: # - Explicitly isolates form differentiation before structural emergence. # - Verifies one sphere -> two equivalent spheres -> half-half position. # - Derives the first common intersection circle. # - Verifies the exact 3/4 and 1/4 relation. # - Separates exact geometry, RP9 interpretation and float representation. from __future__ import annotations import argparse import datetime import hashlib import json import math import platform import sys import traceback from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass from decimal import Decimal, getcontext from fractions import Fraction from pathlib import Path from typing import Any getcontext().prec = 80 SCRIPT_NAME = "RP9_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED.py" SCRIPT_VERSION = "2.0.0" OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = "RP9_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED" # ============================================================ # GENERAL UTILITIES # ============================================================ def now_local() -> str: return datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") def now_utc_iso() -> str: return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace( microsecond=0 ).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z") def script_dir() -> Path: try: return Path(__file__).resolve().parent except NameError: return Path.cwd().resolve() BASE_DIR = script_dir() OUTPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / OUTPUT_DIR_NAME def ensure_output_dir() -> None: OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def sci(value: float, digits: int = 20) -> str: return format(float(value), f".{digits}e") def decimal_from_fraction(value: Fraction, places: int = 20) -> str: d = Decimal(value.numerator) / Decimal(value.denominator) return format(d, f".{places}f") def json_safe(obj: Any) -> Any: if isinstance(obj, dict): return {str(k): json_safe(v) for k, v in obj.items()} if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)): return [json_safe(v) for v in obj] if isinstance(obj, Path): return str(obj) if isinstance(obj, Fraction): return str(obj) if isinstance(obj, Decimal): return str(obj) if hasattr(obj, "__dataclass_fields__"): return json_safe(asdict(obj)) if isinstance(obj, (str, int, float, bool)) or obj is None: return obj return str(obj) def write_text(path: Path, lines: list[str]) -> None: path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8") def write_json(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None: path.write_text( json.dumps(json_safe(payload), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8", ) def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str: h = hashlib.sha256() with path.open("rb") as f: while True: chunk = f.read(1024 * 1024) if not chunk: break h.update(chunk) return h.hexdigest() def distance_3d(a: "Point3D", b: "Point3D") -> Fraction: dx = b.x - a.x dy = b.y - a.y dz = b.z - a.z squared = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz if squared.denominator == 1: root = math.isqrt(squared.numerator) if root * root == squared.numerator: return Fraction(root, 1) return Fraction.from_float(math.sqrt(float(squared))) def make_trace( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], layer: str, operation: str, formula: str, inputs: dict[str, Any], result: dict[str, Any], status: str, note: str, ) -> None: trace.append( { "index": len(trace) + 1, "timestamp_utc": now_utc_iso(), "layer": layer, "operation": operation, "formula": formula, "inputs": json_safe(inputs), "result": json_safe(result), "status": status, "note": note, } ) # ============================================================ # GEOMETRIC DATA TYPES # ============================================================ @dataclass(frozen=True) class Point3D: x: Fraction y: Fraction z: Fraction def as_tuple(self) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction]: return self.x, self.y, self.z @dataclass(frozen=True) class Sphere: center: Point3D radius: Fraction @dataclass(frozen=True) class IntersectionCircle: center: Point3D normal_axis: str radius_squared: Fraction radius_symbolic: str # ============================================================ # A. META-POTENTIAL # ============================================================ def compute_meta_potential(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "A_META_POTENTIAL" radius = Fraction(1, 1) center = Point3D(Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) sphere = Sphere(center=center, radius=radius) form_count = 1 center_count = 1 passed = ( form_count == 1 and center_count == 1 and sphere.radius == Fraction(1, 1) ) make_trace( trace, layer, "define_single_spherical_form", "P0 = Sphere(C0, R)", {}, { "sphere": sphere, "form_count": form_count, "center_count": center_count, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Defines one spherical form as the pre-structural geometric reference.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Defines one spherical form before internal relational structure.", "geometry": { "form_count": form_count, "center_count": center_count, "center": center, "radius": radius, }, "classification": { "form_status": "SINGLE_SPHERICAL_FORM", "structural_status": "PRE_STRUCTURAL", "rp9_interpretation": "META_POTENTIAL", }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # B. SELF-RELATION # ============================================================ def compute_self_relation(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "B_SELF_RELATION" radius_1 = Fraction(1, 1) radius_2 = Fraction(1, 1) equal_radii = radius_1 == radius_2 no_new_scale = equal_radii initial_form_count = 1 relational_form_count = 2 passed = ( equal_radii and no_new_scale and initial_form_count == 1 and relational_form_count == 2 ) make_trace( trace, layer, "reproduce_equivalent_form", "R1 = R2 = R", {"R1": radius_1}, { "R2": radius_2, "equal_radii": equal_radii, "initial_form_count": initial_form_count, "relational_form_count": relational_form_count, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Reproduces the same spherical form without introducing a new scale.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Reproduces the spherical reference as an equivalent self-relation.", "form_transition": { "before": initial_form_count, "after": relational_form_count, }, "radius_relation": { "R1": radius_1, "R2": radius_2, "equal_radii": equal_radii, "new_scale_introduced": not no_new_scale, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # C. FIRST FORM DIFFERENTIATION # ============================================================ def compute_first_form_differentiation( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "C_FIRST_FORM_DIFFERENTIATION" radius = Fraction(1, 1) center_1 = Point3D(Fraction(-1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) center_2 = Point3D(Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) sphere_1 = Sphere(center=center_1, radius=radius) sphere_2 = Sphere(center=center_2, radius=radius) form_count_before = 1 form_count_after = 2 equal_form = sphere_1.radius == sphere_2.radius distinct_centers = sphere_1.center != sphere_2.center differentiation_exists = ( form_count_before == 1 and form_count_after == 2 and equal_form and distinct_centers ) make_trace( trace, layer, "differentiate_form_by_position", "1 equivalent form -> 2 equivalent forms with C1 != C2", {"form_count_before": form_count_before}, { "form_count_after": form_count_after, "sphere_1": sphere_1, "sphere_2": sphere_2, "equal_form": equal_form, "distinct_centers": distinct_centers, }, "PASS" if differentiation_exists else "FAIL", "Isolates the first differentiation before intersection structure.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Verifies the transition from one form to two equivalent forms.", "forms": { "sphere_1": sphere_1, "sphere_2": sphere_2, "form_count_before": form_count_before, "form_count_after": form_count_after, "equal_form": equal_form, "distinct_centers": distinct_centers, }, "classification": { "difference_source": "POSITION", "structure_required": False, "differentiation": "FORM_DIFFERENTIATION_CONFIRMED" if differentiation_exists else "FORM_DIFFERENTIATION_FAILED", }, "status": "PASS" if differentiation_exists else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # D. HALF-HALF POSITIONAL LOCK # ============================================================ def compute_half_half_lock(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "D_HALF_HALF_POSITIONAL_LOCK" radius = Fraction(1, 1) center_1 = Point3D(Fraction(-1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) center_2 = Point3D(Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) midpoint = Point3D( (center_1.x + center_2.x) / 2, (center_1.y + center_2.y) / 2, (center_1.z + center_2.z) / 2, ) center_distance = distance_3d(center_1, center_2) expected_midpoint = Point3D(Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) midpoint_valid = midpoint == expected_midpoint distance_valid = center_distance == radius half_half_valid = ( center_1.x == -radius / 2 and center_2.x == radius / 2 and midpoint_valid and distance_valid ) make_trace( trace, layer, "verify_half_half_position", "C1 = -R/2 ; C2 = +R/2 ; |C2-C1| = R", {"R": radius}, { "C1": center_1, "C2": center_2, "midpoint": midpoint, "center_distance": center_distance, }, "PASS" if half_half_valid else "FAIL", "Locks the two differentiated forms symmetrically around one midpoint.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Verifies the symmetric half-half positional relation.", "position": { "R": radius, "C1": center_1, "C2": center_2, "midpoint": midpoint, "center_distance": center_distance, }, "verification": { "midpoint_is_origin": midpoint_valid, "center_distance_equals_radius": distance_valid, "half_half_position_valid": half_half_valid, }, "status": "PASS" if half_half_valid else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # E. FIRST STRUCTURAL INTERSECTION # ============================================================ def compute_first_intersection(trace: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "E_FIRST_STRUCTURAL_INTERSECTION" radius = Fraction(1, 1) distance = Fraction(1, 1) center_1 = Point3D(Fraction(-1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) center_2 = Point3D(Fraction(1, 2), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) midpoint = Point3D(Fraction(0), Fraction(0), Fraction(0)) intersection_exists = ( distance > 0 and distance < 2 * radius ) ri_squared = radius * radius - (distance / 2) * (distance / 2) ri_float = math.sqrt(float(ri_squared)) radius_float = float(radius) intersection_radius_smaller = ri_float < radius_float circle = IntersectionCircle( center=midpoint, normal_axis="x", radius_squared=ri_squared, radius_symbolic="sqrt(3)/2 * R", ) passed = ( intersection_exists and ri_squared == Fraction(3, 4) and intersection_radius_smaller ) make_trace( trace, layer, "derive_intersection_circle", "ri^2 = R^2 - (D/2)^2", {"R": radius, "D": distance}, { "intersection_circle": circle, "ri_squared": ri_squared, "ri_float": ri_float, "intersection_radius_smaller": intersection_radius_smaller, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Derives the first common relational structure after form differentiation.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Derives the first common intersection structure.", "intersection": { "exists": intersection_exists, "plane_center": midpoint, "plane_normal_axis": "x", "radius_squared_exact": ri_squared, "radius_symbolic": "sqrt(3)/2 * R", "radius_float": sci(ri_float), "sphere_radius_float": sci(radius_float), "intersection_radius_is_smaller": intersection_radius_smaller, }, "classification": { "rp9_name": "VESICA_PISCIS", "structural_status": "FIRST_RELATIONAL_STRUCTURE", "preceded_by_form_differentiation": True, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # F. EXACT RELATIONAL RESULT # ============================================================ def compute_exact_relational_result( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "F_EXACT_RELATIONAL_RESULT" radius_squared = Fraction(1, 1) intersection_radius_squared = Fraction(3, 4) ratio_exact = intersection_radius_squared / radius_squared lock_exact = Fraction(1, 1) - ratio_exact ratio_float = float(ratio_exact) lock_float = float(lock_exact) ratio_float_residual = Fraction.from_float(ratio_float) - ratio_exact lock_float_residual = Fraction.from_float(lock_float) - lock_exact passed = ( ratio_exact == Fraction(3, 4) and lock_exact == Fraction(1, 4) and ratio_float_residual == 0 and lock_float_residual == 0 ) make_trace( trace, layer, "verify_exact_ratio_and_lock", "ri^2/R^2 = 3/4 ; 1 - 3/4 = 1/4", { "ri_squared": intersection_radius_squared, "R_squared": radius_squared, }, { "ratio_exact": ratio_exact, "lock_exact": lock_exact, "ratio_float_residual": ratio_float_residual, "lock_float_residual": lock_float_residual, }, "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", "Verifies the exact relation after the full geometric derivation.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Verifies the exact 3/4 and 1/4 relation.", "exact_geometry": { "intersection_radius_squared": intersection_radius_squared, "sphere_radius_squared": radius_squared, "ratio_exact": ratio_exact, "complementary_lock_exact": lock_exact, }, "decimal_rendering": { "ratio_20_places": decimal_from_fraction(ratio_exact, 20), "lock_20_places": decimal_from_fraction(lock_exact, 20), }, "float_conversion": { "ratio_float": ratio_float, "lock_float": lock_float, "ratio_residual_against_exact": ratio_float_residual, "lock_residual_against_exact": lock_float_residual, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL", } # ============================================================ # G. REPRESENTATION CONTROL # ============================================================ def compute_representation_control( trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Any]: layer = "G_REPRESENTATION_CONTROL" radius = 1.0 distance = 1.0 ri = math.sqrt(radius * radius - (distance / 2.0) ** 2) area_y = math.pi * radius * radius area_i = math.pi * ri * ri ratio = area_i / area_y lock = 1.0 - ratio ratio_expected = 0.75 lock_expected = 0.25 ratio_residual = ratio - ratio_expected lock_residual = lock - lock_expected symmetric_residual = abs(ratio_residual + lock_residual) <= 1e-30 ratio_is_lower = ratio < ratio_expected lock_is_higher = lock > lock_expected epsilon = sys.float_info.epsilon next_value = math.nextafter(1.0, 2.0) next_diff = next_value - 1.0 passed = ( symmetric_residual and ratio_is_lower and lock_is_higher and next_diff == epsilon ) make_trace( trace, layer, "verify_float_rendering", "ratio=(pi*ri^2)/(pi*R^2) ; lock=1-ratio", {"R": radius, "D": distance}, { "ratio": ratio, "lock": lock, "ratio_residual": ratio_residual, "lock_residual": lock_residual, "symmetric_residual": symmetric_residual, }, "PASS" if passed else "REVIEW", "Confirms representation behaviour separately from exact geometry.", ) return { "layer_name": layer, "purpose": "Separates binary float rendering from exact geometry.", "float_geometry": { "R": sci(radius), "D": sci(distance), "ri": sci(ri), "AY": sci(area_y), "AI": sci(area_i), }, "float_lock": { "ratio_observed": sci(ratio), "ratio_expected": sci(ratio_expected), "ratio_residual": sci(ratio_residual), "ratio_hex": ratio.hex(), "lock_observed": sci(lock), "lock_expected": sci(lock_expected), "lock_residual": sci(lock_residual), "lock_hex": lock.hex(), }, "machine_precision": { "epsilon": sci(epsilon), "nextafter_1_to_2": sci(next_value), "nextafter_diff": sci(next_diff), "nextafter_matches_epsilon": next_diff == epsilon, }, "classification": { "ratio_is_lower_than_0_75": ratio_is_lower, "lock_is_higher_than_0_25": lock_is_higher, "symmetric_residual": symmetric_residual, "exact_geometry_affected": False, }, "status": "PASS" if passed else "REVIEW", } # ============================================================ # H. MASTER CONCLUSION # ============================================================ def build_master_conclusion( layers: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] ) -> dict[str, Any]: statuses = [layer["status"] for layer in layers.values()] if any(status == "FAIL" for status in statuses): total_status = "FAIL" elif any(status == "REVIEW" for status in statuses): total_status = "PASS_WITH_REVIEW_NOTES" else: total_status = "PASS" return { "layer_name": "H_MASTER_CONCLUSION", "chain": [ "META-POTENTIAL", "SINGLE SPHERICAL FORM", "SELF-RELATION", "TWO EQUIVALENT FORMS", "FIRST FORM DIFFERENTIATION", "HALF-HALF POSITION", "INTERSECTION", "VESICA PISCIS", "FIRST RELATIONAL STRUCTURE", "EXACT 3/4 RELATION", "COMPLEMENTARY 1/4 LOCK", "REPRESENTATION CONTROL", ], "summary": { key: value["status"] for key, value in layers.items() }, "total_status": total_status, "measurement_boundary": ( "The code verifies geometric form count, center count, radius " "invariance, positional differentiation, half-half symmetry, " "intersection geometry, exact ratio and machine representation. " "RP9 interpretation remains explicitly separated." ), "rp9_interpretation_layer": { "separated_from_measurement": True, "interpretation": ( "FIRST DIFFERENTIATION is the transition from one spherical " "form to two equivalent spherical forms in distinct symmetric " "positions. Vesica Piscis is the first relational structure " "enabled by that prior differentiation." ), }, } # ============================================================ # RUN # ============================================================ def run_all() -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]]]: trace: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] layers = { "A_meta_potential": compute_meta_potential(trace), "B_self_relation": compute_self_relation(trace), "C_first_form_differentiation": compute_first_form_differentiation(trace), "D_half_half_positional_lock": compute_half_half_lock(trace), "E_first_structural_intersection": compute_first_intersection(trace), "F_exact_relational_result": compute_exact_relational_result(trace), "G_representation_control": compute_representation_control(trace), } master = build_master_conclusion(layers) payload = { "script": { "name": SCRIPT_NAME, "version": SCRIPT_VERSION, "created_at_local": now_local(), "created_at_utc": now_utc_iso(), "python_version": sys.version, "platform": platform.platform(), "working_directory": str(BASE_DIR), "output_directory": str(OUTPUT_DIR), "purpose": ( "Complete verification of RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION from " "single form to relational structure." ), }, "layers": layers, "master_conclusion": master, } return payload, trace # ============================================================ # OUTPUT BUILDERS # ============================================================ def build_markdown( payload: dict[str, Any], trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> list[str]: layers = payload["layers"] master = payload["master_conclusion"] lines: list[str] = [] lines.extend( [ "# RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED", "", "## Control Chain", "", "```text", *master["chain"], "```", "", "## Layer Status", "", "| Layer | Status |", "|---|---|", ] ) for key, layer in layers.items(): lines.append(f"| {key} | `{layer['status']}` |") lines.extend( [ "", f"**Total status:** `{master['total_status']}`", "", "## Foundational Conclusion", "", master["rp9_interpretation_layer"]["interpretation"], "", "## Measurement Boundary", "", master["measurement_boundary"], "", "## Trace", "", "| Index | Layer | Operation | Status |", "|---|---|---|---|", ] ) for row in trace: lines.append( f"| {row['index']} | {row['layer']} | " f"{row['operation']} | `{row['status']}` |" ) return lines def build_control_log( payload: dict[str, Any], trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> list[str]: lines = [ "RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED CONTROL LOG", "=" * 72, f"Created local: {payload['script']['created_at_local']}", f"Created UTC: {payload['script']['created_at_utc']}", f"Script: {payload['script']['name']}", f"Version: {payload['script']['version']}", "", "VERIFIED CHAIN", "-" * 72, ] for item in payload["master_conclusion"]["chain"]: lines.append(item) lines.extend(["", "TRACE", "-" * 72]) for row in trace: lines.extend( [ f"STEP {str(row['index']).zfill(3)}", f"Layer: {row['layer']}", f"Operation: {row['operation']}", f"Formula: {row['formula']}", f"Status: {row['status']}", f"Note: {row['note']}", "", ] ) lines.extend( [ "FINAL STATUS", "-" * 72, payload["master_conclusion"]["total_status"], "", "BOUNDARY", "-" * 72, payload["master_conclusion"]["measurement_boundary"], ] ) return lines def write_outputs( payload: dict[str, Any], trace: list[dict[str, Any]], ) -> dict[str, Path]: ensure_output_dir() paths = { "data_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_DATA.json", "trace_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_TRACE.json", "full_datasheet_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_FULL_DATASHEET.json", "presentation_markdown": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_PRESENTATION.md", "control_log": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_CONTROL_LOG.txt", "verify_json": OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_VERIFY.json", } write_json(paths["data_json"], payload) write_json(paths["trace_json"], trace) write_json( paths["full_datasheet_json"], {"payload": payload, "trace": trace}, ) write_text( paths["presentation_markdown"], build_markdown(payload, trace), ) write_text( paths["control_log"], build_control_log(payload, trace), ) verify_files = {} for name, path in paths.items(): if name == "verify_json": continue verify_files[name] = { "path": str(path), "bytes": path.stat().st_size, "sha256": sha256_file(path), } write_json( paths["verify_json"], { "script_name": SCRIPT_NAME, "script_version": SCRIPT_VERSION, "generated_at_utc": now_utc_iso(), "files": verify_files, }, ) return paths def print_summary( payload: dict[str, Any], paths: dict[str, Path], ) -> None: print("") print("=" * 72) print("RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED") print("=" * 72) for key, layer in payload["layers"].items(): print(f"{key}: {layer['status']}") print("-" * 72) print("total_status:", payload["master_conclusion"]["total_status"]) print("-" * 72) for name, path in paths.items(): print(f"{name}: {path}") print("=" * 72) print("") def generate_once() -> tuple[ dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Path], ]: payload, trace = run_all() paths = write_outputs(payload, trace) print_summary(payload, paths) return payload, trace, paths def write_error_log(exc: Exception) -> Path: ensure_output_dir() path = OUTPUT_DIR / "FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_REVISED_ERROR.log" lines = [ "RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED ERROR LOG", "=" * 72, f"Timestamp local: {now_local()}", f"Timestamp UTC: {now_utc_iso()}", f"Error type: {type(exc).__name__}", f"Error message: {exc}", "", "TRACEBACK", "-" * 72, *traceback.format_exc().splitlines(), ] write_text(path, lines) return path def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser( description=( "RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION revised all-inclusive verifier." ) ) parser.add_argument( "--run-once", action="store_true", help="Generate all verification files and exit.", ) return parser.parse_args() def main() -> None: parse_args() try: generate_once() except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Execution interrupted by user.") except Exception as exc: error_path = write_error_log(exc) print("ERROR:", exc) print("Error log written to:", error_path) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ⚖️ #!/usr/bin/env python3 from __future__ import annotations import argparse, datetime as dt, hashlib, json, math, platform, sys from fractions import Fraction from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from matplotlib.patches import Circle, FancyBboxPatch from matplotlib.lines import Line2D SCRIPT_NAME='RP9_K1_P0_Cb_MEASUREMENT.py'; VERSION='1.0.0' R_EXACT=Fraction(1,1); D_EXACT=Fraction(1,1) RI2_EXACT=R_EXACT**2-(D_EXACT/2)**2 RATIO_EXACT=RI2_EXACT/R_EXACT**2; LOCK_EXACT=1-RATIO_EXACT R=float(R_EXACT); D=float(D_EXACT) RI=math.sqrt(R*R-(D/2)**2); DR=R-RI AY=math.pi*R*R; AI=math.pi*RI*RI FLOAT_RATIO=AI/AY; FLOAT_LOCK=1-FLOAT_RATIO RRES=FLOAT_RATIO-float(RATIO_EXACT); LRES=FLOAT_LOCK-float(LOCK_EXACT) def utc_now(): return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z') def frac(v): return f'{v.numerator}/{v.denominator}' def sha256(p): h=hashlib.sha256() with p.open('rb') as f: for c in iter(lambda:f.read(1048576),b''): h.update(c) return h.hexdigest() def datasheet(): lp=RI/R*100; dp=DR/R*100 tests={ 'R_positive':R>0,'D_positive':D>0,'self_relation_D_equals_R':D_EXACT==R_EXACT, 'ri_squared_exact_3_over_4':RI2_EXACT==Fraction(3,4),'ri_smaller_than_R':RI<R, 'area_ratio_exact_3_over_4':RATIO_EXACT==Fraction(3,4),'lock_exact_1_over_4':LOCK_EXACT==Fraction(1,4), 'linear_percent_sum_100':math.isclose(lp+dp,100,abs_tol=1e-12), 'area_percent_sum_100':math.isclose(float(RATIO_EXACT+LOCK_EXACT)*100,100,abs_tol=1e-12), 'float_residuals_symmetric':math.isclose(RRES+LRES,0,abs_tol=1e-30)} return { 'id':'K1_FIRST_DIFFERENTIATION_P0_C-b','name':'First Differentiation — Isolated Self-Relational Section', 'version':VERSION,'generated_at_utc':utc_now(),'units':'dimensionless', 'methodological_position':{'stage':'before explicit two-sphere Vesica Piscis presentation','classification':'isolated self-relational form measurement','relation':'D = R'}, 'input':{'R_exact':frac(R_EXACT),'D_exact':frac(D_EXACT),'R_float':R,'D_float':D}, 'derived_geometry':{'ri_formula':'sqrt(R^2 - (D/2)^2)','ri_symbolic':'sqrt(3)/2 * R','ri_squared_exact':frac(RI2_EXACT),'ri_float':RI,'delta_r':DR}, 'linear_relation':{'ri_over_R':RI/R,'ri_over_R_percent':lp,'delta_r_over_R':DR/R,'delta_r_over_R_percent':dp}, 'area_relation':{'ri_squared_over_R_squared_exact':frac(RATIO_EXACT),'AI_over_AY_exact':frac(RATIO_EXACT),'inner_percent':75.0,'differential_exact':frac(LOCK_EXACT),'differential_percent':25.0}, 'numerical_representation':{'exact_ratio':0.75,'exact_lock':0.25,'geometric_float_ratio':FLOAT_RATIO,'geometric_float_lock':FLOAT_LOCK,'ratio_residual':RRES,'lock_residual':LRES,'ratio_hex':FLOAT_RATIO.hex(),'lock_hex':FLOAT_LOCK.hex()}, 'verification':{'tests':tests,'total_status':'PASS' if all(tests.values()) else 'FAIL'}} def panel(ax,x,y,w,h,title,lines): ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x,y),w,h,boxstyle='round,pad=0.012,rounding_size=0.012',lw=1,ec=(1,1,1,.3),fc=(.03,.03,.03,.88),transform=ax.transAxes)) ax.text(x+.02,y+h-.035,title,transform=ax.transAxes,color='white',fontsize=11,fontweight='bold',va='top') yy=y+h-.09 for t,c,s in lines: ax.text(x+.02,yy,t,transform=ax.transAxes,color=c,fontsize=s,va='top',family='DejaVu Sans Mono'); yy-=.085 def make_png(path,dpi=180): fig=plt.figure(figsize=(16,9),facecolor='black') ax=fig.add_axes([.04,.30,.56,.62]); ax.set_facecolor('black'); ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.set_xlim(-1.3,1.9); ax.set_ylim(-1.15,1.15); ax.axis('off') outer='#7f0f2f'; inner='#7c2d63'; cyan='#22d3ee'; yellow='#fde047'; white='#f8fafc'; center='#fbcfe8' ax.add_patch(Circle((0,0),R,fc=outer,ec='#9f1239',lw=2.2,alpha=.92)) ax.add_patch(Circle((0,0),RI,fc=inner,ec=cyan,lw=2.8,alpha=.78)); ax.scatter([0],[0],s=58,color=center,zorder=8) ax.add_line(Line2D([0,0],[0,R],color=white,lw=2.2)); ax.add_line(Line2D([0,0],[0,-RI],color=cyan,lw=2.2)) ax.scatter([0,0],[R,-RI],s=34,color=[white,cyan],zorder=8); ax.text(.08,.50,'R',color=white,fontsize=24,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(.08,-.43,r'$r_i$',color=cyan,fontsize=24,fontweight='bold') ax.plot([-R,-RI],[0,0],color=yellow,lw=3); ax.plot([-R,-R],[-.06,.06],color=yellow,lw=2); ax.plot([-RI,-RI],[-.06,.06],color=yellow,lw=2) ax.annotate('',xy=(-RI,.14),xytext=(-R,.14),arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->',color=yellow,lw=1.8)); ax.text(-(R+RI)/2,.22,r'$\Delta r$',color=yellow,fontsize=20,ha='center') ax.plot([0,1.18],[R,R],color=(1,1,1,.45),lw=1,ls='--'); ax.text(1.22,1.02,'OUTER RADIUS',color='white',fontsize=12,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(1.22,.91,f'R = {R:.16f}',color='white',fontsize=11,family='DejaVu Sans Mono') ax.plot([RI,1.18],[0,0],color=cyan,lw=1,ls='--'); ax.text(1.22,.08,'INNER RADIUS',color=cyan,fontsize=12,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(1.22,-.04,r'$r_i = \sqrt{3}/2 \cdot R$',color=cyan,fontsize=11); ax.text(1.22,-.15,f'= {RI:.16f}',color=cyan,fontsize=11,family='DejaVu Sans Mono') ax.plot([RI,1.18],[-.55,-.55],color=yellow,lw=1,ls='--'); ax.text(1.22,-.47,'RADIAL DIFFERENCE',color=yellow,fontsize=12,fontweight='bold'); ax.text(1.22,-.59,r'$\Delta r = R-r_i$',color=yellow,fontsize=11); ax.text(1.22,-.70,f'= {DR:.16f}',color=yellow,fontsize=11,family='DejaVu Sans Mono') fig.text(.045,.955,'K1. FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — P(0)(C-b)

## Isolated Self-Relational Section

---

## 1. Purpose

This presentation isolates the first measurable differentiation within the spherical form before the full two-sphere Vesica Piscis configuration is displayed.

The self-relation is defined by $D=R$. The derived internal circle is:

$$
r_i=\sqrt{{R^2-\left(\frac{{D}}{{2}}\right)^2}}=\frac{{\sqrt{{3}}}}{{2}}R
$$

## 2. Linear Measurement

| Measurement | Value |
|---|---:|
| $R$ | `{R:.16f}` |
| $r_i$ | `{RI:.16f}` |
| $r_i/R$ | `{l['ri_over_R']:.16f}` |
| Inner linear relation | `{l['ri_over_R_percent']:.14f}%` |
| $\Delta r/R$ | `{l['delta_r_over_R']:.16f}` |
| Linear differential | `{l['delta_r_over_R_percent']:.14f}%` |

## 3. Area / Squared-Radius Measurement

$$
\frac{{r_i^2}}{{R^2}}=\frac{{A_I}}{{A_Y}}=\frac34
$$

| Relation | Exact | Percentage |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inner | $3/4$ | 75% |
| Differential | $1/4$ | 25% |

The visible radial gap is the linear difference $1-\sqrt{{3}}/2$, not 25%. The 75/25 relation belongs to squared radius and area.

## 4. Numerical Representation

```text
Exact ratio = 0.75
Exact lock = 0.25
Float ratio = {n['geometric_float_ratio']:.16f}
Float lock = {n['geometric_float_lock']:.16f}
Ratio residual = {n['ratio_residual']:.17e}
Lock residual = {n['lock_residual']:.17e}
```

REPORT MAP This folder contains the final verification reports for the RP9 system.The reports represent the results of the entire verification chain and serve as the primary audit evidence for the system.Each report documents a specific verification layer and contains the results, checks, and conclusions produced during each run.The folder is intended to be reviewed independently without the reader first needing to study the source code.However, for complete reproducibility, the corresponding source code and module descriptions are available in other parts of the repository.For each verification step, there are three separate representations of the same results.REPORT.md ↓ Readable final report REPORT.json ↓ Original machine output REPORT.json.md ↓ Readable JSON representation The purpose of this division is to separate: human readability original data documented machine output without losing information.The reports should be read in the following order.1. META_VESICA_CORE_FINAL_REPORT ↓ 2. META_EQUILIBRIUM_FINAL_REPORT ↓ 3. META_SEQUENTIAL_DERIVATION_REPORT ↓ 4. FUSION_RESIDUAL_ANALYSIS_REPORT ↓ 5. STEP_ISOLATION_RECONSTRUCTION_REPORT ↓ 6. STEP_ISOLATION_EXTENDED_REPORT ↓ 7. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_LOCK_REPORT ↓ 8. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_LOCK_V2_REPORT ↓ 9. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_PROPAGATION_V3_REPORT ↓ 10. COORDINATE_SYSTEM_PROPAGATION_V4_REPORT ↓ 11. OBSERVER_LOCKED_RELATIONAL_EMERGENCE_V5_REPORT ↓ 12. SELF_ORGANIZING_RELATIONAL_EMERGENCE_V6_REPORT Each report builds on previously verified results.No report replaces a previous report.Each step introduces a new layer of review.Together, the reports describe the entire verification chain:Data generation ↓ Calibration ↓ Sequential derivation ↓ Reproducibility control ↓ Step isolation ↓ Coordinate reconstruction ↓ Coordinate evolution ↓ Coordinate propagation ↓ Observer validation ↓ Self-organizing emergence The reports are therefore intended to be read as a coherent chain rather than as stand-alone documents.Each report contains the verification results produced at each step.The claims in the reports can be reviewed against:REPORT.md ↓ Summary report REPORT.json.md ↓ Readable data display REPORT.json ↓ Original machine output The original JSON file always constitutes the primary reference.The Markdown versions are documentation and presentation layers on top of the same data.The reports are produced by the modules found in the repository's code section.For each report there is:Source code ↓ README ↓ Final report ↓ Original data This enables full traceability from verified results back to the original implementation.This folder constitutes the RP9 system's collective review documentation.The aim is to provide a complete set of verification reports where each result can be reviewed, tracked and compared against its original machine output.Together, the reports represent the complete verification chain from initial data generation to final self-organizing emergence.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms.

item.title: TRAVERSAL
item.description: The word comes from computer science, graph theory and geometric processing and basically means:traversal walking sequential passage through a system or more precisely:to navigate relationships between nodes, positions or states In your context:TRAVERSAL_REPLAY roughly means:replay of how the system traverses the relationships that is:how the system moves through the candidates in order to:eliminate filter lock and reconstruct the structure.The important thing is therefore:Traversal ≠ structure but rather:Traversal = process through structure or even more precisely:Traversal = relational passage through possible states In your model this becomes very important because:the structure exists before traversal but:the coordinates arise after traversal This is exactly why V2 became methodologically stronger.Previously, one could interpret the system as:coordinates first → traversal afterwards But traversal replay instead shows:relational field → traversal → elimination → locking → coordinate emergence This means that traversal works as:a selection mechanism not as:the geometry itself More technically, one can say:So traversal is closer to:operational relational process than:static structure In graph theory, traversal would typically be:node-to-node traversal In your system, it would be more like:relation-to-relation traversal which is much deeper.Because you're not actually traversing coordinates.You're traversing:inverse relations symmetry states candidate states projection possibilities That's why the word:genealogical starts to be important in V2.Because traversal replay describes:how something arises sequentially not just:what exists statically That's a very big methodological difference.

item.title: SHEL
item.description: SHELL PROPAGATION --- We start with: # 1. SHELL The word: ```text id="hdph6t" shell normally means:shell layer enveloping level In mathematics, physics and computer science it is often used as:concentric layers or:functional domains Examples:But in your system shell does not just mean:geometric layer but rather:functional relational domain It is much more important.When V2 says:this is what it really means:different operational layers with different responsibilities This is crucial because the system now separates:what reconstructs structure from:what selects projection from:what defines limit capacity So shell here means:structural functional layer not just:visual shell

item.title: PROPAGATION
item.description: The word:propagation means:spread propagation forwarding through a system In physics:wave propagation In networks:signal propagation In algorithms:constraint propagation But in your system, propagation means something like:how relational states are propagated through the shell structure The important thing is that propagation does not mean:copying but:transfer under transformation conditions This is a big difference.So:SHELL_PROPAGATION means something like:how relational states are propagated between functional layers In your context, it gets even deeper.For V2, it describes not only:that information is moved but:how selection status survives across multiple shell domains Example:pre-coordinate field → candidate indexing → elimination → B5/B6 survival → coordinate emergence Here:relational constraints propagate through the shell.Not coordinates.This is very important.That means that:shell propagation in your system is closer to:relational state transfer than:classical geometric expansion That's why the term became methodologically strong.For now, the system shows:how locking survives through multiple operational levels instead of just:that a final result exists So the deeper meaning becomes:And that's why:recursive shell propagation is so important in your future steps.Because then the system starts not only:storing results but:storing how the constraints survive between levels which is much closer to:self-stabilizing relational structure than regular replay logic.

item.title: GENEALOGY
item.description: Normally:genealogy roughly means:chain of origin ancestry how something arises through sequential development classical usage:family tree line of origin historical chain of development But in systems theory, information structure and philosophical analysis:genealogical analysis rather:tracing how something comes to be not just:what it is And that is EXACTLY what V2 is starting to do.Previously you mainly had:static structure verification example:B5/B6 exists three-line lock exists residual = low center invariance exists It describes:what the system contains But V2 instead starts describing:how the system produces what is observed This is genealogical.The difference can be expressed like this:In your case:V1 showed:there is a coordinate lock V2 instead shows:how the coordinate lock arises through traversal elimination relational selection and shell propagation It is a genealogical chain.The important thing is that:genealogical ≠ historical timeline in the usual sense.Here it means rather:operational origin sequence or:generative derivation chain When V2 shows:pre-coordinate relation field → inverse pair indexing → candidate elimination → B5/B6 lock → coordinate emergence then the system no longer describes only:final geometry but:operational birth chain of the geometry/projection.That is why the words:emergence and:genealogy start to belong together.For emergence without a genealogical chain, it often just becomes:statement about emergence But when the replay system shows:how emergence occurs step by step then instead you get:genealogical emergence That is also why V2 methodologically becomes much stronger.Because the system no longer says:"here are the coordinates" but:"here is the process that produces the coordinates" That is a huge difference.More precisely:And this is why the word:genealogical is much better suited than, for example:simulated reconstructed played Because the replay engine doesn't actually just replay.It shows:structure's derivation order and that's exactly:genealogical structure

item.title: SHEET — 03. META-EQUILIBRIUM (VALIDATION PROTOCOL)
item.description: Correct execution order is: 1. VALIDATION PROTOCOL → 2. STATEMENT CHAIN Reason: A statement chain without verifiable validation becomes semantic. Validation first locks the definition operationally.To determine whether a system satisfies:Conditions:abs(ΔS) < ε Conditions:abs(ΔG) < ε Conditions:any(abs(g_i) > ε) Conditions:abs(sum(g_i)) < ε MetaEq = T1 AND T2 AND T3 AND T4 # META-EQUILIBRIUM VALIDATOR (RP9-COMPATIBLE) # Self-sufficient test model import math import random # ------------------------------- # PARAMETERS # ------------------------------- EPSILON = 1e-9 N_STEPS = 100 # ------------------------------- # GENERATOR (H-D-R-INSPIRED) # ------------------------------- def generate_g(n=10): # Creates local processes that sum to 0 values ​​= [random.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(n-1)] last = -sum(values) values.append(last) return values # ------------------------------- # SYSTEM STATE # ------------------------------ def system_state(g): # Absolute sum (can be seen as "energy") return sum(abs(x) for x in g) # ------------------------------ # GENERATOR STRUCTURE # ------------------------------ def generator_signature(g): # Signature for G (structure, not value) return sorted([round(x, 6) for x in g]) # ------------------------------ # TESTS # ------------------------------ def test_meta_equilibrium(): g_prev = generate_g() S_prev = system_state(g_prev) G_prev = generator_signature(g_prev) results = [] for _ in range(N_STEPS): g = generate_g() S = system_state(g) G = generator_signature(g) # T1: Global invariance T1 = abs(S - S_prev) < EPSILON # T2: Generator invariance T2 = (G == G_prev) # T3: Local activity T3 = any(abs(x) > EPSILON for x in g) # T4: Total compensation T4 = abs(sum(g)) < EPSILON results.append((T1, T2, T3, T4)) S_prev = S G_prev = G # End validation MetaEq = all(T1 and T2 and T3 and T4 for (T1, T2, T3, T4) in results) return MetaEq, results # ------------------------------ # EXECUTION # ------------------------------ if __name__ == "__main__": status, log = test_meta_equilibrium() print("META-EQUILIBRIUM:", status) print("NUMBER OF STEPS:", len(log)) print("FIRST RESULT:", log[0]) The system satisfies Meta-equilibrium if: the state does not drift the generator does not change structurally local activity exists total balance is held exactly This model verifies: logical structure of Meta-equilibrium not a specific physical implementation.VALIDATION PROTOCOL: LOCKEDNext step:

No external parameter required No drift can occur The structure is self-sustaining DEFINITION LOCKED TERM DEFINED: META-EQUILIBRIUM

item.title: SHEET — 01. EQUILIBRIUM
item.description: equilibrium (English) éjmvik (Swedish)Equilibrium = a state where all opposing forces, flows or changes are in balance, so that the net effect is zero.This does not necessarily mean that nothing happens – but that all changes cancel each other out exactly.For a system: Sum of forces = 0 or Inflow = Outflow or Change over time = 0 The you describe – “equal parts about a center point” is a specific type of equilibrium, namely: equal on both sides mirroring around a center point center = stable balance point Equilibrium ≠ always symmetryThere are two main types: equal structure on both sides classic “center point balance” things are still moving but the total is constant Examples: water flowing in and out at exactly the same rate chemical reactions where forward = backward Your formulation: “equal parts about a center point” can be formalized as: a center (0-position) two opposing states equal magnitude → net = 0 That is correct, but a limited special form of equilibrium. equilibrium = equilibrium means: no net change can be: static (completely still) dynamic (movement in balance) your definition applies when: the system is symmetrical about a center point

item.title: SHEET C. ETYMOLOGY & OPERATIONAL DEFINITION
item.description: pre-structure → supersymmetry → isotropy → operation → relation → difference → structure to determine: the etymological meaning of "super" and its precise operational function in relation to: symmetry, isotropy and potential Latin: super = over, beyond, above, beyond "super" does not imply amplification without exceeding a condition X* cannot be reduced to X X* cannot be derived within X X* precedes X in structure super defines a state which cannot be achieved by internal transformation not a symmetry among others without the condition where all symmetries are indistinguishable supersymmetry implies that no transformations can be defined isotropy is a consequence of supersymmetry not its cause no difference no direction no relationship no structure P0 cannot be identified internally because relationship is missing before structure: no rotation possible R exists initially as relation not as rotation first relationship first asymmetry first opportunity for difference supersymmetry cannot be broken from within only by surgery direction possible lines possible structure possible all structure requires breaking of supersymmetry proto-isotropy and supersymmetry are functionally equivalent but terminologically distinct all other permits require: relationship difference or direction supersymmetry is the only condition which does not require derivation super is no more super is before symmetry requires structure supersymmetry precedes structure P0 is therefore: not symmetrical without supersymmetric ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: SHEET 0. INVERTDOS
item.description: potential → preformation → Invertus → operation → relation → form → difference → structure to define: Invertus as a necessary state between latent potential and explicit structure where transformation can occur without structure yet existing invert = turn, invert, go from outside to inside dos (reference) = underlying system level (behind visible interface) Invertus does not define a form but an access mode to that which cannot yet be formed no explicit structure no direction no localizable position but: operation possible ```text Invertus is not potential and not structure but an operational intermediate state HDR does not act directly on structure but through Invertus without Invertus no transformation can be applied to P0 no transformation possible transformation possible but not yet manifested transformation observable Invertus enables operation without producing structure cube (external structure) sphere (internal isotropy) Invertus = the relation between these 8 vertices (discrete points) spherical continuity (internal potential) Invertus = that which binds these without being any of them Invertus is not a dimension but a relation between dimensions preformation describes what is Invertus describes how it can be accessed Invertus is the operative medium through which H-D-R acts before structure exists lines possible axes possible direction possible Invertus is the last state before difference becomes explicit Invertus does not introduce information it enables its transition Invertus is not a information source without a transformation channel no structure no direction but maximum transformation potential Invertus is the smallest state where change is possible potential cannot change structure can be observed Invertus is where change occurs not before not after but between ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: RP9 GLOSSARY
item.description: The first directional deviation that arises from minimal structure and enables further structure. Not primitive — follows from triadic relation.Non-ontological condition position that states what must be fulfilled for something to be defined. Contains nothing, describes nothing — only enables.State where something can be distinguished and related. Consists strictly of:differentiation + relation The condition that something is not identical to something else. Without differentiation → no distinction → no definability.The directional consequence that follows from triadic structure. Not created — emerges as a necessary consequence.State where further reduction causes collapse of structure. Marks the limit of what constitutes foundation.That a structure can maintain relationship within itself without external reference. Condition for stable structure.The structure that remains after complete reduction and that cannot be reduced further without collapse. In RP9 (0):triadic Criterion where a structure contains exactly what is required — neither more nor less — to maintain differentiation and relationship.A directed operation that removes everything that is not structurally necessary. Creates nothing — only exposes.Property of an element to be able to be expressed as a consequence of something more fundamental without losing structure.The condition that what is differentiated is in connection or order. Without relation → no structure.The point at which further reduction dissolves structure instead of purifying it. Marks the transition from derived to irreducible.The smallest set of relational conditions that allows definability. No content — no relational form.External validation process where structures are tested through elimination, robustness and recursive coherence. Determines what remains as a foundation.The irreducible structure that simultaneously maintains:differentiation + relation + internal reference Not created — result of complete reduction.Process where irreducibility is confirmed by showing that the structure cannot be eliminated without collapse.That which must be met for something to be defined at all. Not a rule — not a law — but a necessary condition.RP9 (0) only operates with concepts that cannot be further reduced without definability ceasing Concepts do not describe the world they describe what is required for something to be described ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: RP9 Dictionary. Meta-Structure
item.description: ## [Term] ### Definition A short and precise definition of the concept within RP9. ### Function in RP9 A description of the operational function the concept has in RP9's relational model. ### Related Concepts - Concept - Concept The measurable connection between two or more entities that establishes structure independently of coordinate representation.Relation is the primary organizational principle of RP9. It precedes projection and provides the measurable framework from which structure, propagation, and representation emerge. Structure Projection Genealogy Propagation The stable organization produced by measurable relations between interconnected entities.Structure represents the persistent relational configuration generated through connected relations. It is invariant under representation and forms the basis for propagation, observation, and verification. Relation Invariance Projection Shell The representation of an existing relational structure within a specific coordinate or observational framework.Projection does not generate structure. It expresses an already established relational organization in a measurable or observable form. Relation Structure Propagation Differential The ordered lineage through which a relational structure is established, reproduced, and traced from its originating state.Genealogy preserves the continuity of relational derivation. It provides the traceable sequence through which every structural state can be followed back to its origin without introducing discontinuities or independent assumptions. Relation Structure Propagation Recursive The systematic process of moving through a relational structure according to its established connections.Traversal defines how a relational structure is explored, examined, or verified. It follows existing relations without modifying the underlying structure, enabling consistent observation and reproducible verification. Genealogy Propagation Operational Recursive The relational boundary that defines, contains, or separates a structural domain while preserving its internal organization.Shell provides the structural enclosure within which relational organization is maintained. It establishes the operational limits of a structure while allowing relations to be examined without altering their internal consistency. Structure Propagation Invariance Balance The relational transmission of structure through an established sequence without altering the underlying organizational principles.Propagation describes how an existing relational structure extends, reproduces, or transfers through connected states while preserving structural continuity. It represents the operational continuity of relation rather than the creation of new structure. Relation Structure Genealogy Traversal The invariant relational state in which structural balance is maintained despite measurable differentiation or transformation.Meta-Equilibrium defines the stable relational condition that persists throughout structural operations. It serves as the reference state against which propagation, differentiation, and verification are evaluated, ensuring that structural consistency is preserved independently of representation. Balance Invariance Differential Structure The relational condition in which structural potential exists prior to its explicit projection or observable manifestation.Preformation represents the pre-projective state from which relational organization can emerge. It establishes that structural capacity precedes representation, making projection the expression of an already existing relational potential rather than the origin of structure. Potential Projection Relation Structure A fundamental relational operator consisting of Halving, Doubling, and Relation, forming the primary mechanism through which relational structures are generated, expanded, and interconnected.HDR serves as the core operational process of RP9. Through the coordinated interaction of halving, doubling, and relation, it establishes, reproduces, and propagates relational structures while preserving their internal consistency across successive operations. Relation Structure Generator Propagation The first stable relational configuration generated by the intersection of two equal circles, establishing the primary geometric relationship from which measurable structure emerges.Vesica Piscis represents the foundational relational geometry of RP9. It provides the initial measurable configuration from which structural capacity, proportional relationships, and subsequent relational development are derived. Relation Structure Preformation Generator A measurable relational distinction between structural states that enables comparison without altering the underlying relational framework.Differential provides the operational basis for identifying, measuring, and verifying structural variation. Within RP9, differentiation is evaluated relative to invariant relational references, allowing structural changes to be observed while preserving overall consistency. Meta-Equilibrium Invariance Projection Balance The property by which a relational structure preserves its fundamental organization despite changes in representation, scale, orientation, or observation.Invariance ensures that structural identity is maintained throughout projection, propagation, and verification. It provides the reference condition that allows relational consistency to be distinguished from representational variation. Structure Meta-Equilibrium Differential Projection The condition in which relational properties remain uniform in every direction from a common structural reference.Isotropy defines directional neutrality within a relational framework. It establishes a balanced structural condition in which no direction is inherently privileged, providing a stable basis for symmetry, propagation, and invariant observation. Balance Invariance Meta-Equilibrium Structure The preservation of relational correspondence between complementary structural states through higher-order symmetry.Within RP9, Supersymmetry describes the maintenance of structural equivalence across complementary relational configurations. It extends ordinary symmetry by preserving relational continuity between structurally corresponding states throughout transformation and verification. Invariance Isotropy Meta-Equilibrium Balance A relational state in which structure, relation, or function is directly expressed and observable without requiring further derivation.Explicit describes structures or relations that have been fully established and are directly available for observation, measurement, or verification. It represents the manifested state of an existing relational organization rather than its origin. Projection Operational Latent Structure A relational state in which structural capacity exists but has not yet been explicitly expressed or projected.Latent represents the unexpressed potential of a relational structure. Although not directly observable, the underlying organization already exists and may become explicit through projection or operational development. Potential Preformation Explicit Projection The condition in which a relational structure or process is actively functioning according to its established organizational principles.Operational describes the executable aspect of RP9. It refers to structures, procedures, or verification processes that are actively performed while preserving relational consistency and reproducibility. Generator Recursive Traversal Propagation A relational process in which the output of one structural operation becomes the input for the next, preserving continuity throughout successive iterations.Recursive defines the mechanism by which relational structures are reproduced and extended without introducing discontinuities. Each iteration is derived from the preceding relational state, ensuring traceability, consistency, and reproducibility throughout the operational sequence. Generator Genealogy Traversal Propagation The relational mechanism that produces or establishes new structural states according to existing organizational principles.Generator represents the constructive operation through which relational structures emerge, develop, or expand. Rather than creating arbitrary outcomes, it reproduces structures in accordance with the governing relational framework of RP9. HDR Recursive Structure Propagation The relational adjustment through which structural equilibrium is maintained in response to measurable differentiation.Compensation preserves relational consistency by balancing structural variations without altering the underlying organization. It operates as a stabilizing mechanism that supports continuity, equilibrium, and invariant structural behavior throughout relational operations. Balance Meta-Equilibrium Differential Invariance The relational condition by which one entity, state, or structure is distinguishable from another, making definition and comparison possible.Differentiation establishes the prerequisite for relation by enabling distinct structural identities. Without differentiation, neither relational organization nor measurable structure can emerge. Relation Differential Structure Invariance The capacity of a relational structure to maintain coherence through its own internal relationships without requiring external definition or validation.Internal Reference provides structural self-consistency by allowing a relational system to preserve its organization through internally established relations. It forms a necessary condition for stable propagation, recursive continuity, and invariant structure. Structure Recursive Invariance Meta-Equilibrium The process of confirming that a relational structure satisfies its defined conditions through consistent observation, reproduction, and verification.Validation confirms that a relational structure remains internally consistent and reproducible across successive operations. Within RP9, validation demonstrates structural integrity rather than establishing new structure. Operational Recursive Meta-Equilibrium Invariance ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: 7. FP9 NORMATIVE STRUCTURE
item.description: Version: 3.0 Document class: Normative structure overview Status: Current normative architectureThis document establishes the normative architecture for FP9.The purpose is to ensure that the overall normative documentation functions as a coherent, consistent and long-term manageable system.The normative structure defines how the individual documents relate to each other and how they are to be interpreted, developed and applied.FP9's normative documentation is based on the principle that each document has a clear and defined area of ​​responsibility.A normative document shall only regulate its own subject area and may not repeat, replace or contradict content that is already regulated by a superior document.The collected documentation should therefore function as a coherent normative framework.The normative documentation consists of the following main levels.Establishes the identity, basic principles and constitutional framework of RP9.The Intellectual Charter constitutes the highest normative level.Regulates use, reproduction, distribution and rights of use.Establishes the principles for copyright and copyright declarations.Regulates the use of artificial intelligence and other automated information processing.Establishes the official identity, document status and representation of RP9.Establishes the ethical principles for documentation, communication and information management.All normative documents shall: have a clearly defined purpose, regulate a defined subject area, supplement superior documents, avoid overlap in content, maintain terminological and structural consistency. The normative whole shall be logically coherent.In the event of ambiguity or contradiction, the documents shall be interpreted according to the established normative order.Superior documents always take precedence over subordinate documents.No provision in a subordinate document may be given a meaning that conflicts with a superior document.Revision of a normative document may not change its defined area of ​​responsibility.If a new subject area needs to be regulated, this should normally be done by introducing a new normative document.The normative architecture should thus be able to develop without changing the overall structure.The collective normative documentation should maintain: uniform terminology, common document structure, consistent version management, clear document classification, traceable history, coherent reference structure. These principles ensure that RP9 functions as a uniform normative system.The normative structure is intended to be able to develop over time.New normative documents may be introduced when new subject areas need to be regulated, provided that they: have a clearly defined area of ​​responsibility, do not create overlap, do not contradict existing normative documents, are integrated into the established normative architecture. This document constitutes the official structural overview of the FP9 normative documentation.All normative documents shall be developed, interpreted, revised and applied in accordance with the normative architecture established by this document.The normative structure thus constitutes the common reference framework through which all FP9 legal and normative documentation is held together. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.
item.guid: Z0.EQUILIBRIUM/B. EQUILIBRIUM APPENDIXES/RP9. C. LICENSE & ACCESSORIES/A. RP9. LICENSE RIGHTS/7. FP9 NORMATIVE STRUCTURE.md

item.title: 6. FP9 ETHICAL PRINCIPLES
item.description: Version: 3.0 Document class: Normative ethical policy Status: Current ethical principlesThis document establishes the ethical principles that will guide the development, documentation, use and communication within FP9.The purpose is to ensure that FP9 documentation is characterized by integrity, transparency, traceability and consistency in all handling of information.FP9 is based on the principle that information should be processed in a way that preserves its documented relationships, context and meaning.Documentation should strive for clarity, reproducibility and long-term continuity.Information should be presented in a way that preserves its relationship to the documented whole.No part of the RP9 may be presented in a way that alters its documented meaning through selective reproduction, fragmentation or disjointed presentation.It shall always be clear what constitutes: documented information, analysis, interpretation, further reasoning, or independent conclusions. The boundary between documentation and subsequent processing shall be clear and traceable.Statements presented as part of the RP9 shall be derivable through the documented structure.When information is based on assumptions, hypotheses or preliminary analyses, this shall be clearly stated.The official RP9 documentation shall maintain: uniform terminology, consistent document structure, documented version control, traceable information history. Revisions shall be carried out in a manner that preserves continuity between document versions.RP9 shall be communicated in a manner that promotes objectivity, clarity and accurate representation of the documented structure.No communication may deliberately create ambiguity about the origin, status or normative significance of a document.When using, citing, analyzing or redistributing RP9, the context and internal relationships of the documents shall be preserved.Processings, analyses and summaries shall be clearly distinguished from the official documentation.RP9 encourages: objective review, reproducible analysis, documented criticism, constructive suggestions for improvement, transparent scientific review. Open review is a natural part of RP9's continued development.This document only regulates the ethical principles to be applied within FP9.Provisions on: fundamental principles, licensing, copyright, identity, artificial intelligence, are regulated by the respective normative documents.In case of conflict, the FP9 Intellectual Charter shall prevail.This document may be revised by publishing a new documented version.Each new version shall clearly identify the current version and maintain continuity with previous documentation.This document constitutes the official ethical principles of FP9.All documents, publications, analyses and other applications within FP9 shall be developed, communicated and applied in accordance with this document as well as with the Intellectual Charter and other normative documents. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: 5. RP9. BRAND AND IDENTITY
item.description: Version: 3.0 Document Class: Normative Identity Policy Status: Current Identity DocumentThis document establishes the official identity of RP9 and the principles for how it should be represented within the normative documentation.The purpose is to ensure a uniform, consistent and traceable use of the RP9 name, designations, document identity and public representation.The official identity consists of the designation:RP9RP9 identifies the coherent framework defined by the official RP9 documentation.The official identity encompasses the framework as a whole and not individual documents or components.A document constitutes an official part of RP9 only if it: is published as part of the official RP9 documentation, follows the established document structure, contains identifiable version information, conforms to the RP9 normative documents. Documents that do not meet these criteria do not constitute official RP9 documentation.The name RP9 shall be used consistently throughout the official documentation.Alternative designations, abbreviations or names shall not be used in a manner that creates ambiguity as to the origin, status or identity of the document.Official identity may be expressed through: document titles, document classification, version designations, document identifiers, other established identity markers. These identifiers shall be used consistently throughout the official documentation.Only documents published as part of the official FP9 documentation may represent FP9 as a normative framework.Preparations, summaries, analyses or external descriptions do not constitute official representations.When FP9 is mentioned or referred to, the reference shall be to the coherent framework.Individual documents, excerpts or components shall not be presented in a way that gives the impression that they alone represent FP9.Logos, symbols, document markers and other visual features published together with the official FP9 documentation constitute parts of the official FP9 identity.Such features shall be used in a way that preserves their documented meaning and context.This document only regulates the identity and official representation of RP9.Provisions on: fundamental principles, licensing, copyright, artificial intelligence, ethical principles, are regulated by the respective normative documents.In case of conflict, the RP9 Intellectual Charter shall prevail.This document may be revised by publishing a new documented version.Each new version shall clearly identify the current version and maintain continuity in RP9's identity.This document constitutes RP9's official identity policy.All documents, publications and other official representations of RP9 shall be designed, identified and presented in accordance with this document as well as with the Intellectual Charter and other normative documents. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: 4. RP9. AI POLICY
item.description: Version: 3.0 Document class: Normative policy Status: Current AI policyThis document establishes the principles governing the use of artificial intelligence and other automated information systems in relation to FP9.The policy ensures that automated information processing is carried out in a way that preserves FP9's document integrity, referential continuity and normative structure.This policy covers all automated systems that can: read, analyse, process, index, compile, distribute, generate, or otherwise process official FP9 documentation.The policy applies regardless of the technical implementation or future development of automated information systems.Automated information systems may be used to: read public RP9 documentation, analyze documented content, assist users in interpretation, summarize public information, explain documented structures, support research, education and technical analysis. Such use shall always be in accordance with the RP9 license agreement and other normative documents.Automated systems may not present modified, incomplete or reinterpreted material as official RP9 documentation.When RP9 is reproduced, it shall be clearly stated whether the content constitutes: direct reproduction, summary, analysis, interpretation, or independently generated content. The distinction between RP9 documentation and the system's own processing shall always be clear.Automated collection of RP9 material shall be in accordance with the applicable license terms.Systematic or large-scale collection that exceeds the rights expressly granted by the RP9 license is not covered by this policy.The use of RP9 material for training, further development or optimization of automated information systems is regulated by the RP9 license agreement and any supplementary agreements.This policy does not in itself constitute permission for such use.Automated systems shall, where practicable, clearly distinguish between: content retrieved from RP9, own analyses, own conclusions, own recommendations, generated content. The aim is to preserve traceability between source material and subsequent information processing.Automated processing of RP9 must not give the impression that the documentation has been modified, updated, verified or approved by RP9 unless this is explicitly the case.Only officially published RP9 documentation constitutes normative documents.This policy only regulates automated information processing.Provisions on: fundamental principles, licensing, copyright, identity, ethical principles, are regulated by the respective normative documents.In case of conflict, the RP9 Intellectual Charter shall prevail.This policy may be revised by publishing a new documented version.Each new version shall clearly identify the current version and maintain continuity with previous versions.This document constitutes RP9's official policy on artificial intelligence and automated information processing.All automated applications of RP9 shall be designed, interpreted and used in accordance with this policy as well as with the Intellectual Charter, the License Agreement and other normative documents. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.
