item.title: RP9. Invariant Logic. Extended Edition
item.description:
Note A1 — Explanatory Support This document follows the RP9 A1 standard. This document follows the RP9 A1 standard and acts as a human interface to the formal documentation. A1 does not introduce any new axioms, relations or verifications, but acts as a human interface between the formal presentation and the technical verification. APPENDIXES only explain and visualize already verified information. The Primary Calibration established that the RP9 framework can derive, reproduce, and computationally verify a complete relational architecture. Having demonstrated reproducibility, the next methodological question concerns invariance itself. Specifically, under what conditions does a relational structure remain unchanged while its observable representations vary?This section addresses that question by separating structural organization from its numerical, geometric, and computational manifestations.Primary Calibration demonstrated that a complete relational framework can be generated, reproduced, and independently verified. The objective of the present section is fundamentally different. Rather than constructing additional geometry or introducing new computational procedures, it examines the logical principles that explain why the established framework remains invariant despite changes in representation.The central proposition is that relational organization and observable representation belong to different descriptive layers. Numerical values, geometric projections, coordinate systems, computational precision, and visual configurations all describe the framework from different observational perspectives. None of these representations constitutes the structure itself. Instead, they serve as alternative manifestations of an underlying relational organization whose internal connectivity remains unchanged.This distinction is methodologically essential. Classical mathematical analysis often concentrates on measured quantities: numerical constants, coordinate values, lengths, areas, and derived equations. RP9 instead emphasizes the relational role performed by those quantities within the structural organization. The numerical value becomes secondary to the function it performs inside the relational system. Consequently, invariant structure is defined not by immutable numbers but by preserved relational connectivity.The implications extend throughout the framework. The emergence of the first differentiation, the establishment of the 3/4 relational proportion, recursive H-D-R reproduction, Core4 generation, Meta-Equilibrium, computational verification, and coordinate propagation all become specific observational manifestations of the same invariant relational architecture. Each verification presented previously therefore represents an independent observation of one continuous structural genealogy rather than a separate mathematical result.This perspective also clarifies the role of computational verification. Floating-point residuals, machine epsilon, binary precision, and numerical approximations belong exclusively to the representational layer. They quantify the limits of numerical encoding without modifying the relational organization being represented. Machine precision therefore measures the boundary of representation rather than the validity of the underlying structure itself.Accordingly, invariance becomes an observable property of relational continuity rather than numerical permanence. A structure may be projected through different coordinate systems, visualized at different scales, reproduced through independent computational paths, or subjected to different observational classes while preserving identical relational organization. What changes is the description; what remains invariant is the organization that those descriptions represent.The following chapters investigate this principle systematically. Beginning with the distinction between structure and representation, the section progressively demonstrates that invariant relational organization explains the stability observed across geometric construction, computational verification, recursive propagation, coordinate emergence, and long-term structural continuity.The opening chapter establishes the conceptual separation upon which the remainder of the section depends. Before examining invariant geometry, recursive propagation, or computational verification, it is first necessary to distinguish the relational architecture itself from the numerical and geometric representations through which it becomes observable. This distinction provides the logical foundation for every subsequent demonstration in the Invariant Logic sequence.
Primary Calibration introduced the RP9 framework through two complementary methodological domains. The S-Series establishes the conceptual and relational derivation of the framework, while the K-Series independently reconstructs the same relational architecture through executable computational verification. Neither series replaces the other; together they form a synchronized methodology in which conceptual derivation and machine verification remain continuously aligned throughout the entire framework.The RP9 framework is intentionally divided into two synchronized methodological layers. Although each series operates through different methods, both investigate the same underlying relational architecture from complementary perspectives.The S-Series constitutes the conceptual layer of the framework. Its purpose is to derive the relational principles that define the structure before any computational implementation is introduced. Through sequential conceptual development, the framework establishes the minimal relational conditions required for structural differentiation, recursive reproduction, and observational organization. Each sequence extends the previous one without introducing discontinuities, thereby constructing a logically continuous relational genealogy.The K-Series performs the complementary computational function. Rather than proposing new concepts or extending the theoretical framework, it independently reconstructs each conceptual result through deterministic computation. Every relational statement established within the S-Series is translated into executable procedures whose outputs can be reproduced, audited, and verified under controlled numerical conditions. The code therefore functions as an independent verification layer rather than a source of new theoretical content.This separation serves an important methodological purpose. Conceptual derivation and computational verification remain independent processes while continuously converging upon identical relational conclusions. The framework therefore avoids circular reasoning, since conceptual propositions are not validated by themselves but are reconstructed through an entirely different operational methodology.The synchronization between both layers establishes a bidirectional correspondence throughout the framework. S1 is reproduced by K1 through basic relational verification. S2 is reconstructed by K2 through recursive structural generation. S3 is independently confirmed by K3 through operational verification and observational consistency. Each conceptual milestone therefore possesses a corresponding computational counterpart that can be reproduced independently while preserving the same relational organization.Because both methodological layers operate independently yet produce identical structural outcomes, reproducibility becomes substantially stronger than simple numerical agreement. The framework demonstrates that invariant relational organization is recoverable regardless of whether one begins with conceptual derivation or computational reconstruction. The agreement between the two methodologies therefore constitutes evidence of methodological consistency rather than merely computational accuracy.This synchronized architecture also defines the organizational principle for the remainder of the repository. Conceptual exposition and computational verification remain distinct throughout every subsequent section, allowing each methodological layer to perform its respective function without conflating theoretical interpretation with executable verification.Having established the complementary roles of conceptual derivation and computational verification, the next chapter examines the fundamental distinction upon which both methodologies depend. Before relational structures can be derived or verified, it is necessary to distinguish invariant structure from the variable representations through which that structure becomes observable.
Classical mathematics primarily characterizes geometric objects through measurable quantities. Numerical constants describe lengths, ratios, angles, and areas that can be calculated with arbitrary precision. RP9 adopts a complementary perspective. Rather than asking what a numerical value is, the framework asks what structural role that value performs within an invariant relational organization. This distinction separates numerical representation from relational function while preserving the validity of both approaches.The distinction introduced in this chapter defines one of the fundamental methodological principles of the RP9 framework. Throughout mathematics, numerical constants are typically understood through their measured values. The diagonal of a unit square is represented by √2, the circumference of a circle through π, proportional growth through φ, and the first stable relational equilibrium through the proportion 3/4. These numerical values constitute accurate descriptions of observable geometry, but they do not by themselves explain why those geometric relationships exist.RP9 therefore introduces a second descriptive layer. Instead of treating mathematical constants exclusively as numerical quantities, the framework interprets them according to the structural function they perform within an invariant relational architecture. The numerical value remains unchanged, but its methodological role shifts from representation to organization.This distinction is illustrated consistently throughout the examples presented. The value √2 is not regarded merely as an irrational decimal expansion but as the structural operation responsible for diagonal differentiation. Likewise, π is understood not simply as a transcendental constant but as the relational function describing continuous surface representation. The golden ratio becomes a mechanism of proportional expansion rather than merely a numerical proportion. Finally, the 3/4 relation is interpreted as the irreducible relational equilibrium from which the first stable structural differentiation emerges.Importantly, RP9 does not replace numerical mathematics with relational interpretation. Both descriptions coexist, but they answer fundamentally different questions. Numerical representation quantifies observable geometry, whereas relational analysis identifies the organizational principles responsible for that geometry. One describes the measurable outcome; the other describes the invariant relational mechanism producing it.This separation also explains why invariant structure can survive changes in numerical representation. Decimal approximations, floating-point encodings, coordinate systems, and computational precision belong entirely to the representational layer. Their values may vary according to measurement or machine implementation while the relational function remains completely unchanged. Consequently, structural invariance depends upon preserved relational organization rather than identical numerical encoding.Within the RP9 methodology, this perspective becomes increasingly important as the framework develops toward recursive generation, coordinate emergence, Meta-Equilibrium, and computational verification. This invariant pair continues to satisfy every previously established relational constraint, allowing the entire coordinate architecture to recover a globally coherent state.The accompanying verification ledger summarizes this result.The statementconfirms that every required central structural condition survives the deformation.Likewise,demonstrates that the defining relational lock remains intact despite the extensive topological mutation.This outcome has important methodological implications.The experiment does not claim that geometric form is immutable.Instead, it demonstrates that relational identity survives transformations that substantially alter observable appearance. Structure is therefore defined by invariant relational continuity rather than by fixed geometric configuration.Within the RP9 framework, successful recovery is consequently not measured by returning to an identical visual arrangement. It is measured by preserving the complete relational genealogy that generated the structure in the first place.The recovered field therefore represents considerably more than a repaired coordinate network.It constitutes experimental evidence that recursive relational organization possesses sufficient internal coherence to maintain structural identity through dynamic topological evolution without requiring external intervention or manual recalibration.Having demonstrated that relational continuity survives substantial internal deformation, the remaining step is to integrate every verification stage into a single computational audit.The following chapter assembles the complete verification pipeline, showing how the entire RP9 framework progresses from initial relational potential to a fully reproducible, machine-verifiable system whose structural continuity is preserved across every stage of derivation, mutation, and observation.
The preceding sections establish an invariant relational framework together with an independently reproducible computational verification chain. The final step is to distinguish the structure itself from the different layers through which it is observed, represented, and interpreted.This distinction defines the methodological boundary of the RP9 framework.RP9 distinguishes between three fundamentally different levels of description.The Measurement Layer contains numerical observations generated by computational systems. Floating-point residuals, numerical approximations, and machine precision belong exclusively to this level. They describe how a computer represents a relation, not the relation itself.The Representation Layer converts relational information into observable geometry. Coordinates, projections, diagrams, and symbolic notation belong here. Representation provides a visual or numerical description of structure but remains dependent upon perspective, scale, and implementation.The Interpretation Layer assigns conceptual meaning to the represented structure. Mathematical models, theoretical descriptions, and explanatory language all exist within this layer. Interpretation may change over time without modifying the underlying relational organization.RP9 therefore separates these three domains explicitly.Measurement records numerical manifestations.Representation visualizes structural organization.Interpretation explains the observed organization.None of these layers defines the relational structure itself.Instead, each layer projects the same invariant relational framework from a different methodological perspective.Within this architecture, the structural relation remains constant while numerical values, graphical representations, and conceptual interpretations may all vary independently.This separation allows computational verification to remain independent from theoretical interpretation while preserving complete traceability between both domains.Consequently, RP9 treats relational structure as the invariant reference against which every measurement, representation, and interpretation is evaluated.With the methodological architecture established, the Primary Calibration concludes. The remaining sections extend this invariant relational framework into the Secondary Verification, where independent computational pathways reproduce, audit, and stress-test the same relational architecture under increasingly complex conditions. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: RP9. Invariant Logic 02
item.description: Note A1 — Explanatory Support This document follows the RP9 A1 standard. This document follows the RP9 A1 standard and acts as a human interface to the formal documentation. A1 does not introduce any new axioms, relations or verifications, but acts as a human interface between the formal presentation and the technical verification. APPENDIXES only explain and visualize already verified information. Primary Calibration introduced the RP9 framework through two complementary methodological domains. The S-Series establishes the conceptual and relational derivation of the framework, while the K-Series independently reconstructs the same relational architecture through executable computational verification. Neither series replaces the other; together they form a synchronized methodology in which conceptual derivation and machine verification remain continuously aligned throughout the entire framework.The RP9 framework is intentionally divided into two synchronized methodological layers. Although each series operates through different methods, both investigate the same underlying relational architecture from complementary perspectives.The S-Series constitutes the conceptual layer of the framework. Its purpose is to derive the relational principles that define the structure before any computational implementation is introduced. Through sequential conceptual development, the framework establishes the minimal relational conditions required for structural differentiation, recursive reproduction, and observational organization. Each sequence extends the previous one without introducing discontinuities, thereby constructing a logically continuous relational genealogy.The K-Series performs the complementary computational function. Rather than proposing new concepts or extending the theoretical framework, it independently reconstructs each conceptual result through deterministic computation. Every relational statement established within the S-Series is translated into executable procedures whose outputs can be reproduced, audited, and verified under controlled numerical conditions. The code therefore functions as an independent verification layer rather than a source of new theoretical content.This separation serves an important methodological purpose. Conceptual derivation and computational verification remain independent processes while continuously converging upon identical relational conclusions. The framework therefore avoids circular reasoning, since conceptual propositions are not validated by themselves but are reconstructed through an entirely different operational methodology.The synchronization between both layers establishes a bidirectional correspondence throughout the framework. S1 is reproduced by K1 through basic relational verification. S2 is reconstructed by K2 through recursive structural generation. S3 is independently confirmed by K3 through operational verification and observational consistency. Each conceptual milestone therefore possesses a corresponding computational counterpart that can be reproduced independently while preserving the same relational organization.Because both methodological layers operate independently yet produce identical structural outcomes, reproducibility becomes substantially stronger than simple numerical agreement. The framework demonstrates that invariant relational organization is recoverable regardless of whether one begins with conceptual derivation or computational reconstruction. The agreement between the two methodologies therefore constitutes evidence of methodological consistency rather than merely computational accuracy.This synchronized architecture also defines the organizational principle for the remainder of the repository. Conceptual exposition and computational verification remain distinct throughout every subsequent section, allowing each methodological layer to perform its respective function without conflating theoretical interpretation with executable verification.Having established the complementary roles of conceptual derivation and computational verification, the next chapter examines the fundamental distinction upon which both methodologies depend. Before relational structures can be derived or verified, it is necessary to distinguish invariant structure from the variable representations through which that structure becomes observable. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: SHEET 3. Potential — etymology
item.description: The word comes from:potentiaMeaning:power ability power capacity to act posseposse = to be able, to be able to This in turn consists of: potis = powerful, capable esse = to be Thus:posse = to be capable of being From posse is formed:potentia = the state of being able It is therefore not the action — but the capacity before action. Latin: potentia French: potentiel English: potential Potential = that which can be but is not yet realized In classical ontology (e.g. Aristotle):potential (dynamis) vs actual (energeia) Etymologically, “potential” means:a state that contains capacity without yet having manifested form potentia ← posse ← (potis + esse) = capacity to be = possibility of form = non-actualized structure ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: SHEET 1. Preformation
item.description: The word preformation is a classically compound Latin term. It can be broken down exactly like this:Preformation ← Latin: prae = before, before, in advance formare = to shape, shape, give structure formatio = formation, creation of form More strictly: "pre-formation" or "structure that already exists before the process of development begins" The etymology carries a very clear ontological position: Form precedes the process Development = expansion, not construction No new structure arises — only scaling In preformation theory, this means exactly: The organism is already fully structured Embryogenesis = geometric/quantitative growth Not: differentiation or emergence epi- = on top, addition genesis = origin, coming into being Preformation = form before process Epigenes = form through process Translating this into a strict relational framework: Preformation assumes that: Structure = static and complete from the start Operators (processes) = passive scaling functions Epigenesis assumes that: Structure = derived through relational operations Form = result of sequence (H–D–R-like dynamics) ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

INDEX. B. RP9. ETYMOLOGY & RELATIONAL FOUNDATIONS The RP9 Dictionary provides the standardized terminology used throughout the RP9 framework.Its purpose is to establish a consistent conceptual language by defining the primary terms, their operational functions, and—where necessary—their etymological and relational foundations.The Dictionary serves as the common reference for all documentation within the repository and ensures that each technical term is interpreted consistently across the entire RP9 framework.The Dictionary is organized into two complementary sections.This section contains the official RP9 terminology.Each concept is defined using a standardized structure consisting of: Definition Function in RP9 Related Concepts These definitions constitute the primary reference vocabulary used throughout the repository.Its purpose is standardization rather than interpretation.This section provides the extended conceptual foundation behind selected RP9 terms.Rather than introducing new terminology, it explains: linguistic origin etymological development operational interpretation relational derivation structural context These documents establish why a concept is defined as it is and how it functions within the relational architecture of RP9.The two sections serve different but complementary purposes.Primary Terms & Definitions answer the question: What does this term mean within RP9? Etymology Definition answers the question: Why is this term defined this way, and how is it relationally derived? Together they provide both a standardized terminology and the underlying conceptual framework supporting that terminology.The RP9 Dictionary is not intended to function as a general scientific glossary.Only concepts that have a direct operational function within the RP9 framework are included.General scientific terminology is referenced only when required to establish the relational meaning of an RP9 concept.Within the RP9 repository, the Dictionary functions as the central terminological reference.Its purpose is to ensure that all documentation uses a consistent vocabulary, allowing concepts, validation procedures, and structural descriptions to remain semantically aligned throughout the entire RP9 framework.RP9 DictionaryRepository Terminology ReferenceFormally Standardized ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

SECOND DIFFERENTIATION Harmonic Probe. PYTHON K6 constitutes the concluding module of the RP9 code-based verification framework.Where the previous verification modules establish, reproduce, validate and test the invariance of the relational structure, K6 demonstrates that additional observable phenomena can be positioned within the same verified relational architecture without modifying the underlying structure.Rather than introducing new relational principles, K6 extends the operational application of the existing framework.Its purpose is to demonstrate that previously verified relations remain sufficient to describe further operational observations.K6 performs the second operational differentiation of the RP9 framework.Beginning from the relational structure established throughout K1–K5, the module introduces an additional observational layer while preserving the complete relational organisation.The operational sequence can be summarized as:Established Structure ↓ Verified Invariance ↓ Second Differentiation ↓ Operational Positioning ↓ Relational Observation ↓ Verification The objective is not to generate a new structure, but to demonstrate that further observable quantities can be positioned within the same invariant relational framework.K6 represents the final operational layer of the RP9 verification sequence.Previous modules demonstrate that the relational structure can be: established, reproduced, verified, and shown to remain invariant. K6 extends this sequence by demonstrating that additional operational phenomena can be incorporated without altering the verified relational organisation.The emphasis therefore shifts from structural validation to relational positioning.K6 investigates whether additional operational quantities preserve the relational continuity established throughout the previous verification chain.Among the verified properties are: second relational differentiation, harmonic positioning, binary-triadic pulse continuity, seven-pass continuity, fine-structure positioning, machine residual consistency, operational reproducibility. Each verification examines whether the observed quantity occupies its expected position within the previously established relational framework.The operational chain follows the verified sequence:First Differentiation ↓ Half-Half Relation ↓ Binary-Triadic Pulse ↓ Seven Passage ↓ Fine Structure Constant ↓ Machine Residual ↓ Operational Verification Each layer depends upon the successful verification of the previous layer.No individual quantity is evaluated independently.Each observation is interpreted only within the established relational sequence.The complete verification chain becomes:K1 Primary Structure ↓ K2 Computational Reproduction ↓ K3 Relational Observation ↓ K4 Operational Verification ↓ K5 Structural Invariance Testing ↓ K6 Operational Positioning Each module extends the previous verification.No module replaces earlier results.K6 therefore represents the final operational extension of the verified framework.K6 does not: redefine the relational structure, introduce new structural principles, derive independent mathematical laws, replace previous verification modules. Instead, it demonstrates that previously established relational structures remain sufficient to position additional operational observations.The K6 package contains: operational source code, structured datasets, execution logs, reproducible presentations, verification reports, complete audit material. Every computational result may therefore be independently reproduced and verified.K6 concludes the RP9 code-based verification framework.Rather than introducing additional structural assumptions, the module demonstrates that further operational observations—including harmonic relations, binary-triadic behaviour, seven-pass continuity, the positioning of the fine-structure constant, and machine-level residuals—can all be incorporated into the same invariant relational architecture established by the preceding verification modules.Accordingly, K6 serves as the final operational confirmation that the RP9 framework remains internally consistent throughout the complete verification chain.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms.

PYTHON This code constitutes the eighth and final verification in the RP9 sequence.All previous tests have verified relations, quotients, pulse structures and reconstruction properties through exact rational arithmetic.The purpose of the final test is to investigate what happens when the same structure is projected down into the machine's floating point storage.The focus is therefore shifted from:Relation to:Representation and from:Exact structure to:Machine representation The goal is to determine whether the observed:1/3 ↔ 2/3 -pulse can still be identified when expressed as IEEE-754 floating point.The code generates the sequence:q(n) = (3/4) / 2^n and:8 / q(n) for:40 iterations At each iteration, the:integer part and:remainder Then the:1/3 and:2/3 are verified against:float representation to measure the residual between:exact rational value and:machine-represented value In addition verified:2^-49 ↔ 2^-52 to check the previously identified quotient:8 in the machine store.Previous tests have shown that:3/4 produce a stable pulse:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... However, these tests have mainly been performed with exact rational arithmetic.This test instead examines:What does the machine see? The question is no longer:Is the relation correct? but:How is the relation represented in the floating-point store? The test therefore functions as a bridge between:Exact mathematics and:Machine representation Basic relation:3/4 Operation model:q(n) = (3/4) / 2^n Check operation:8 / q(n) Number of iterations:40 Expected pulse:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... Verifications:1. Residue sequence 2. Float representation 3. Residue size 4. Residue order 5. Quotient between 2^-49 and 2^-52 If the model is correct, it is expected:All iterations PASS and:2/3 for even n 1/3 for odd n The residual is expected to be:non-zero because:1/3 and:2/3 cannot be represented exactly as IEEE-754 floating point numbers.In addition, it is expected that:2^-49 / 2^-52 = 8 to give an exact result.Number of iterations:40 Result:Residual sizes:1/3 ≈ −1.850371707708594 × 10^-17 2/3 ≈ −3.700743415417188 × 10^-17 Residual order:10^-17 Machine limit:2^-52 = 2.220446049250313e−16 2^-49 = 1.776356839400250e−15 Ratio:2^-49 / 2^-52 = 8 All checks:PASS The test passed.The observed:1/3 ↔ 2/3 -pulse survives all the way down to the machine layer.The machine does not represent:1/3 or:2/3 exactly.However, the residuals arise consistently and reproducibly.The result therefore shows that:The relation is preserved The representation is approximated and that:The residual is measurable, traceable and reproducible. In addition, it is verified again:1/8 ↔ 8 by:2^-49 / 2^-52 = 8 which gave an exact result.When run, the following is generated:rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe.py ├── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe_run_trace.json ├── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe_execution.log └── rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe_FINAL REPORT.md The JSON file contains:Full run trace All iterations Residual data Machine limits Verification status The log file contains:Start time End time Exit code The Markdown file contains:Complete final report This is the final verification in the recommended running order:1. rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test 2. rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check 3. rp9_start_independence_test 4. rp9_base_independence_test 5. rp9_perturbation_test 6. rp9_reverse_test 7. rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test 8. rp9_333_666_float_boundary_probe The eight tests verify together:Origin ↓ Pulse ↓ Start-independent ↓ Base-independent ↓ Disruption resistance ↓ Reversibility ↓ Quota locking ↓ Machine representation The last test therefore serves as the final link between:Relational structure and:Actual machine representationentation of the same structure. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

PYTHON This code constitutes the seventh verification in the RP9 sequence.The previous tests have verified:R ↓ Rx8 ↓ 3/4 ↓ 1/3 ↔ 2/3 This verification instead focuses on the ratio that recurs throughout the chain:1/8 ↔ 8 The purpose is to determine whether this ratio remains exactly invariant through repeated scale steps and can thus serve as a stable lock value within the model.The code generates the sequence:R(0) = 1 R(n+1) = R(n) / 8 For each level, the following are verified:R(n+1) / R(n) and:R(n) / R(n+1) The requirement is that these should always give:1/8 respectively:8 without deviation.Previous tests have shown that:3/4 produces a stable pulse.This test instead examines the underlying scaling relation.The question is:Is the ratio 1/8 ↔ 8 a consequence of single examples or is it invariant throughout the sequence? If the ratio remains exactly locked through all levels, the hypothesis that:1/8 ↔ 8 constitutes a fundamental scaling relationship in the tested model is strengthened.Starting value:R(0) = 1 Iteration:R(n+1) = R(n)/8 Verifications per level:R(n+1)/R(n) and:R(n)/R(n+1) Number of levels:101 Fit conditions:R(n+1)/R(n) = 1/8 and R(n)/R(n+1) = 8 for all levels.If the hypothesis is correct:1/8 returns at each downscaling.At the same time:8 return at each upscaling.Expected outcome matrix:Number of verified levels:101 Result:In addition, it was verified that:R16 / R15 = 1/8 R15 / R16 = 8 which also gave:PASS without deviation.The test was passed.The ratio:1/8 ↔ 8 remained exactly invariant through all verified levels.No iteration broke the relation.The result shows that:R(n+1)/R(n) and:R(n)/R(n+1) form an exactly reversible ratio structure within the investigated area.When executed, the following is generated:rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test.py ├── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test.json ├── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test.log └── rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test_FINALRAPPORT.md The JSON file contains all verified levels.The log file contains the execution history.The markdown file contains the summary verification report.The first seven tests have now verified:1. B. Reverse Test. FINAL REPORT Link — 🔗. B. Reverse Test. FINAL REPORT C. Reverse Test. PYTHON Link — 🔗.
C. Reverse Test. PYTHON This code constitutes the sixth verification in the RP9 sequence.The previous tests have examined the forward structure:R ↓ Rx8 ↓ 3/4 ↓ 1/3 ↔ 2/3 This test reverses the direction.The purpose is to examine whether the observed residual pulse can be used to deduce possible original values.The test therefore serves as the first verification of the reversibility of the sequence.The code starts from the previously observed pulse sequence:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... Then a large number of possible candidate values ​​are tested:q = a/b to determine which ones reproduce exactly the same pulse.For each candidate, the following is performed:8 / (q / 2^n) during:8 iterations If the remainder follows:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... the candidate is accepted.If the sequence is broken, the candidate is rejected.Previous tests have shown that:3/4 produces the observed residual pulse.This test examines the opposite question:If we only know the pulse, can we find the relationship? The test is therefore used to determine whether the pulse sequence contains sufficient information to reconstruct possible original values.Search range:1 ≤ numerator ≤ 64 1 ≤ denominator ≤ 64 Total number of candidates tested:4096 Fit condition:residual sequence = 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 over all:8 iterations Candidates that meet the condition are saved.Other candidates are discarded.If the pulse sequence is reproducible in reverse, it is expected that:at least one valid candidate is identified.If the sequence is also relationally stable, it is expected that:3/4 will be found among the approved candidates.Expected final status:PASS Number of candidates tested:4096 Number of candidates that reproduced the pulse:53 Among these were found:3/4 and several relationally closely related candidates.Example:3/64 3/31 3/16 3/10 3/7 3/4 3 12 All of these reproduced the observed pulse sequence within the limits of the test.Final status:PASS The test passed.The observed pulse sequence can be used to identify candidate values ​​that reproduce the same behavior.The result shows that:pulse ↓ candidatevalue is possible as an operation.This verifies that the sequence not only works forwards but can also be analyzed backwards.The test does not prove that:3/4 is the only possible candidate.However, the test shows that:3/4 is included in the set of values ​​that exactly reproduce the observed pulse within the tested range.When run, the following is generated:rp9_reverse_test │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_reverse_test.py ├── rp9_reverse_test.json ├── rp9_reverse_test.log └── rp9_reverse_test_FINALREPORT.md The JSON file contains all identified candidates.The log file contains the run history.The Markdown file contains the summary verification report.The first six tests have now verified:1. Origin reconstruction 2. Pulse invariance 3. Start independence 4. Base independence 5. Perturbation resistance 6. Reversibility The next step will be:rp9_quotient_lock_1_over_8_test Where the focus shifts from:relations to:quotients The question changes from:Can the sequence be run backwards? to:Is the quotient 1/8 ↔ 8 invariant throughout the system? This will be the first direct verification of the quotient locking that recurs throughout the RP9 sequence. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

C. Binary Pulse Invariance Check. PYTHON This code is the second verification in the RP9 chain.After the previous test has shown that different representative R values ​​can be normalized to the same structure, this code examines whether the resulting pulse is stable over time.The purpose is to determine whether the alternation:1/3 ↔ 2/3 is a temporary numerical effect or a reproducible invariant structure.The code starts from the relation:3/4 and generates the sequence:q_n = (3/4) / 2^n For each iteration, the following is calculated:8 / q_n Then the following is extracted: the integer part the remainder The remainder is then compared against:1/3 2/3 and the expected change:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... over 100 iterations.If the observed pulse is truly a structural feature, it must survive repeated iterations.The test therefore examines:3/4 ↓ (3/4)/2^n ↓ 8/q_n ↓ remainder to determine whether:1/3 ↔ 2/3 is invariant.If the pulse breaks at any iteration, there is no support for treating it as a stable structure.If the pulse never breaks, the hypothesis that it is a recurring feature of the operation under investigation is strengthened.Input value:3/4 Operation:q_n = (3/4) / 2^n Check:8 / q_n Iterations:100 Fit conditions:remainder ∈ {1/3, 2/3} and:even n -> 2/3 odd n -> 1/3 Exact rational arithmetic is used through:fractions.Fraction which eliminates rounding errors during the verification itself.If the hypothesis is correct, it is expected that: all iterations pass the remainder be 1/3 or 2/3 the alternation follow the same pattern throughout the test no iteration breaks the sequence Expected final status:PASS The result was:During all iterations it was observed:2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 ... without interruption.The test was passed.For the investigated operation:3/4 ↓ (3/4)/2^n ↓ 8/q_n produces a residual pulse that remains invariant through all verified iterations.The result shows that the pulse does not occur as a single numerical outcome but as a reproducible property of the tested sequence.When run, the following is generated:rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check.py ├── rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check_SLUTRAPPORT.md └── rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check_run_trace.json The JSON file contains the complete run history.The Markdown report contains the verification result.The Python file contains the reproducible test implementation.This verification shows that the pulse exists and remains stable through iteration.The next question becomes:Does it matter how 3/4 is represented? Therefore continue to:rp9_start_independence_test There it is verified whether the same pulse arises from:3/4 6/8 12/16 24/32 48/64 ... and thus whether the structure is independent of starting resolution and representation. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

C. R. Origin Reconstruction Test. PYTHON This code constitutes the first verification in the RP9 chain.The purpose is to investigate whether the relational structure can be reproduced without depending on a specific absolute starting value.The test is based on the assumption that an original value:Rdoes not need to function as an absolute measurement, but instead as a relational reference that can be reconstructed by the operation:R → R × 8The goal is to determine whether the same structure reappears regardless of which representative R value is used.The code tests the following chain:R ↓ R × 8 ↓ (R × 8) / R ↓ 8 ↓ 3/4 ↓ 1/3 ↔ 2/3For each chosen R value, it is verified that: R is multiplied by 8. The result is normalized by dividing by the same R. The normalization gives the exact value 8. The value 8 is used together with the representation 3/4. The resulting residual pulse alternates between: 2/3 1/3 2/3 1/3 over all iterations.Other verifications in the code package assume that the representation 3/4 already exists.This code therefore fulfills a special function:It verifies the step before the representation.The question being investigated is:Can the same structure be reproduced from different R-values ​​without changing the result?If the answer is yes, it means that: R serves as a reference. R is normalized away. The relational structure is preserved. The test therefore serves as a bridge between:origin ↓ representationand the subsequent verifications in the package.The following representative R-values ​​are used:For each value, the following is performed: Calculation of R × 8. Normalization according to: (R × 8) / R Verification that the result is exact: 8 Generation of the sequence: 8 / ((3/4) / 2ⁿ) Check that the residual values ​​alternate between: 2/3 ↔ 1/3during 40 iterations.If the hypothesis is correct, it is expected: All R values ​​are reduced to the same normalized value. Normalized Rx8 is always 8. The same pulse occurs for all R values. None of the iterations break the pattern. Expected final status:PASSAll tested R values ​​gave:Example:The result shows that the same structure is reproduced regardless of the chosen R-value.The test was passed.For all representative R values, the following applies:R ↓ R × 8 ↓ 8and the same residual pulse:2/3 ↔ 1/3recurs during all iterations.The code results therefore support the hypothesis that the investigated structure is not dependent on a specifically chosen R value, but on the relational operation performed on the value.When run, the following is generated:rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test │ ├── README.md ├── rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test.py ├── rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test.json ├── rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test.log └── rp9_R_origin_reconstruction_test_FINALRAPPORT.md The JSON file contains complete traceability.The log file contains the run history and final status.The markdown report contains the detailed verification report.This verification establishes that:R ↓ R × 8 ↓ 8is reproducible and independent of the chosen R value.The next step is to investigate whether the resulting structure produces a stable pulse.Therefore, proceed to:rp9_binary_pulse_invariance_check There it is verified whether the relation:1/3 ↔ 2/3remains invariant through repeated iterations. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

Residual Validator therefore introduces a clear separation between:Relation and Representation This layer ensures that:The residual is not misinterpreted as new information. Instead, it verifies that the residual is only:A trace of the representation. PYTHON This code constitutes the third layer in the Rx8 STRUCTURE BASE.After:GENEALOGY has verified the chain of origin andPROPORTION has verified the preservation of proportion,this validator examines how the relational chain develops into concrete structural layers.The purpose is to verify that all structures can be derived from previously verified layers without introducing a new primary relation.The code verifies:STRUCTURE This means that the focus is on:Shape Geometry Encapsulation Classification Development chains The central question is:Can the structure be derived from the already verified relation and proportion chain? The validator performs eight verifications:1. Vesica Piscis 2. Bitromb 3. Triangle → Square 4. Square → Cube 5. 7 + 1 locking 6. A/B/C classes (6-6-8) 7. 4 → 10 → 20 8. Global structural traceability chain The controlled development chain is:Relation ↓ Representation ↓ Proportion ↓ Vesica Piscis ↓ Bithrombus ↓ Triangle → Square ↓ Square → Cube ↓ 7 + 1 ↓ 6 - 6 - 8 ↓ 4 → 10 → 20 The previous two validators ensured:Where from the structure will and that the proportion is preserved This layer instead answers:How the structure is built up. Without this verification, it would be possible to:Accept structures without knowing whether they are actually derived from previous layers. The Structure Validator therefore implements the following check:All structures must be traceable. No structure may serve as a new origin. The verification is based on a successive structural development:RELATION ↓ PROPORTION ↓ VESICA PISCIS ↓ BITROMB ↓ TRIANGLE → SQUARE ↓ SQUARE → CUBE ↓ 7 + 1 ↓ 6 - 6 - 8 ↓ 4 → 10 → 20 Each level is examined with respect to:Derivation Internal consistency Proportion conservation Traceability Discipline of origin Finally, all levels are compiled into:GLOBAL STRUCTURAL TRACE CHAIN For the validator to be approved, the following is required:Vesica Piscis ri² = 3/4 Cover = 1/4 and:Bithrombus 2 triangles 4 outer edges Furthermore, it is required:3 → 4 4 → 8 7 + 1 = 8 6 + 6 + 8 = 20 4 → 10 → 20 In addition, all structures must satisfy:Derived structure Not primary relation Expected final status:PASS All eight verifications were approved.Important observations:ri² = 3/4 Lock = 1/4 Bithrombus = 2 triangles 3 → 4 4 → 8 7 + 1 = 8 6 + 6 + 8 = 20 4 → 10 → 20 None of the verified structures introduced a new primary relation.The validator was approved.The result shows that all verified structures can be traced back to previous layers:Relation ↓ Proportion ↓ Structure without:Create new relationship Break traceability Losing derivation PHASE 3 thus confirms that the structure functions as an evolution of previously verified layers and not as an independent origin.When run, the following is generated:RP9_RX8_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR_OUTPUT ├── RP9_RX8_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR.py ├── rp9_rx8_structure_data.json ├── rp9_rx8_structure_trace.json ├── rp9_rx8_structure_audit.json ├── rp9_rx8_structure_verify.json ├── rp9_rx8_structure_presentation.md └── rp9_rx8_structure_control_log.txt Role distribution:DATA = structure data TRACE = audit trail AUDIT = audit layer VERIFY = machine verification PRESENTATION = readable report CONTROL LOG = execution history Next validator is:RP9_RX8_RESIDUAL_VALIDATOR If Structure Validator answers:How is the structure built? then the next layer answers:What remains when the structure is projected into the machine layer? The transition is therefore:GENEALOGY ↓ PROPORTION ↓ STRUCTURE ↓ RESIDUAL which constitutes the next step in Rx8 STRUCTURE BASE. ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

The validator performs six verifications:1. Relational inference 2. Representational inference 3. Geometric encapsulation through Rx8 4. Proportion preservation 5. Residual position 6. Global proportional invariance The chain checked is:1/3 ↔ 2/3 ↓ 1/4 ↔ 3/4 ↓ 2R × 4 = 8R ↓ 0.25 ↔ 0.75 ↓ Residual trace The Genealogical Validator ensured that each layer had the correct origin.This layer instead examines:Whether the same proportion survives throughout the structure. Without this verification it would be possible that: ```text The derivation is correct but the proportion changes. The Proportion Structure Validator therefore introduces the following check:The structure may change The proportion may not change. The verification is built in five layers:RELATION ↓ REPRESENTATION ↓ STRUCTURE ↓ PROPORTION ↓ RESIDUAL For each layer the following is verified:Conclusion Proportion Internal consistency Layer position Traceability Finally all results are compiled in:GLOBAL_PROPORTION_INVARIANCE which is only approved if all previous tests pass.For the validator to be approved, it is required that:1/3 + 2/3 = 1 and:1/4 + 3/4 = 1 It is also required that:2R × 4 = 8R and that:3/4 ↔ 1/4 is preserved as:0.75 ↔ 0.25 The residual must also behave as:Representational trace and not as:New relation Expected final status:PASS All six verifications were approved.Important observations:1/3 + 2/3 = 1 1/4 + 3/4 = 1 2R × 4 = 8R 0.75 + 0.25 = 1.0 The residual check showed:−1.1102230246251565 × 10^-16 + 1.1102230246251565 × 10^-16 = 0 which verified symmetrical residual balance.The validator was approved.The result shows that the same proportional identity is preserved by:Relation ↓ Representation ↓ Rx8 ↓ Residual No verified part of the chain introduces:New proportion New relation New origin position PHASE 2 thus confirms that the structure changes while the proportion remains invariant according to the validator's criteria.When run, the following is generated:RP9_RX8_PROPORTION_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR_OUTPUT ├── RP9_RX8_PROPORTION_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR.py ├── rp9_rx8_proportion_structure_data.json ├── rp9_rx8_proportion_structure_trace.json ├── rp9_rx8_proportion_structure_audit.json ├── rp9_rx8_proportion_structure_verify.json ├── rp9_rx8_proportion_structure_presentation.md └── rp9_rx8_proportion_structure_control_log.txt Role distribution:DATA = verification data TRACE = test chain AUDIT = audit layer VERIFY = machine verification PRESENTATION = readable report CONTROL LOG = execution history The next validator is:RP9_RX8_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR If the Genealogical Validator answered:Where does the structure come from? This code constitutes the first layer in the Rx8 STRUCTURE BASE.The purpose is to verify that all subsequent layers in the model can be derived from a common origin relation and that no subsequent construction is incorrectly assigned the status of origin.The validator thus functions as the genealogical lock for the entire Rx8 chain.The code verifies:GENEALOGY This means that the focus is on:Origin ↓ Derivation ↓ Representation ↓ Reconstruction ↓ Residual and not on numerical optimization or external reference systems.The code verifies six key checkpoints:1. Position of the first relation 2. Derivation of the first representation 3. That the representation does not create a new relation 4. Rx8 as a reconstruction 5. Residual layer position 6. That no later layer claims original status The chain checked is:RELATION 1/3 ↔ 2/3 ↓ REPRESENTATION 1/4 ↔ 3/4 ↓ RX8 2R × 4 = 8R ↓ RESIDUAL Representational trace Without a genealogical verification, later constructions can be misinterpreted as original relations.This layer therefore imposes the following rule:Relation before projection which means that:Relation ↓ Representation ↓ Rx8 ↓ Residual must remain a derivation chain.No subsequent node may:1. Lack derivation 2. Claim origin 3. Replace the first relation The verification is based on four defined layers:RELATION REPRESENTATION RECONSTRUCTION RESIDUAL For each layer, the following is verified:Source of derivation Layer status Origin claim Internal consistency The code generates:DATA TRACE AUDIT VERIFY PRESENTATION CONTROL LOG which makes the entire control chain traceable and reproducible.For the test to pass, it is required that:RELATION_ORIGIN_1 is the only node that is allowed to carry:PRIMARY_ORIGIN_RELATION and that:REPRESENTATION_1 RX8_CAPSULATION_1 RESIDUAL_1 all have valid derivations and lack the ability to claim origin status.Expected final status:PASS All six verification steps passed:The audit report shows:Expected number of origin relations: 1 Observed number of origin relations: 1 Later layers claiming origin: 0 Final status:PASS The validator passed.The result shows that:1/3 ↔ 2/3 remains the only defined origin relation.The representation:1/4 ↔ 3/4 remains derived.Rx8 remains reconstruction.The residual remains representation trace.No later structure introduces a new primary relationship.The genealogy is thus locked according to the validator's criteria.When run, the following is generated:RP9_RX8_GENEALOGICAL_VALIDATOR_OUTPUT ├── RP9_RX8_GENEALOGICAL_VALIDATOR.py ├── rp9_rx8_genealogical_data.json ├── rp9_rx8_genealogical_trace.json ├── rp9_rx8_genealogical_audit.json ├── rp9_rx8_genealogical_verify.json ├── rp9_rx8_genealogical_presentation.md └── rp9_rx8_genealogical_control_log.txt Each file represents a separate audit layer:DATA = structured data TRACE = audit trail AUDIT = audit control VERIFY = machine verification PRESENTATION = human readable report CONTROL LOG = execution trace The next validator is:RP9_RX8_PROPORTION_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR If the Genealogical Validator answers the question:Where does the structure come from? then the next layer answers:Is the proportion preserved throughout the structure? Link — 🔗. INDEX. K2. A. Group Link — 🔗.
INDEX. K2. B. Group Link — 🔗.
INDEX. K2. C. Group K2. CODE & VALIDATION constitutes the primary computational reproduction layer of the RP9 framework.Where A. RP9. PRIMARY CALIBRATION establishes the relational structure through sequential derivation, K2 reproduces that same structure through computational implementation, structural expansion, and operational validation.Its purpose is not to introduce new relational principles.Its purpose is to demonstrate that the established relational framework can be reproduced through a complete, traceable, and reproducible computational architecture.K2 performs five primary methodological functions: reproduce the established relational structure, extend the H-D-R operational sequence through successive structural generations, generate complete relational datasets, document every computational step required for reproduction, establish the computational foundation for subsequent verification. Together these functions transform the documented relational framework into a fully reproducible computational environment.Within the RP9 repository, K2 occupies the first operational layer of Secondary Verification.Its position within the overall presentation architecture is:0. RP9. INTRODUCTION ↓ A. RP9. PRIMARY CALIBRATION ↓ K2. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K4. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K5. CODE & VALIDATION ↓ K6. CODE & VALIDATION Primary Calibration establishes the relational structure.K2 demonstrates that the same structure can be reproduced computationally without altering the underlying relational organization.K2 develops the established framework through several successive operational stages.The general computational sequence is:Relational Structure ↓ H-D-R Generation ↓ Structural Expansion ↓ Node Networks ↓ Complete Structural Models ↓ CORE×4 Development ↓ Computational Documentation ↓ Operational Validation Each stage extends the previous one while preserving the same invariant relational structure.No stage replaces an earlier stage.The repository is organised into three primary computational domains.The foundation layer contains the computational infrastructure required to execute the complete K2 environment.It includes: execution systems, master runners, export systems, metadata generation, full structural exports, and supporting computational resources. This layer develops the H-D-R sequence through successive operational generations.The structure progresses through:(H-D-R) ×1 ↓ (H-D-R) ×2 ↓ (H-D-R) ×3 Each generation expands the previously established relational structure through: Form, Nodes, Structure, computational implementation, JSON datasets, and supporting appendices. Rather than introducing new structures, each level reproduces the same relational principle through increasing structural complexity.The final computational layer reproduces the complete structural capacity of the framework.This includes: CORE×4 construction, X-Y-Z structural propagation, intersection generation, coordinate relations, complete structural datasets, extended validation, and large-scale observational data. This layer represents the complete operational reproduction of the relational framework established during Primary Calibration.Primary Calibration establishes the invariant relational structure through sequential derivation.K2 demonstrates that the same structure can be reproduced computationally through deterministic operational procedures.Accordingly, K2 should be understood as a computational reproduction of an already established framework rather than an independent derivation.Documentation establishes the structure.K2 reproduces the structure.Later verification stages examine the reproduced structure.Every computational result generated within K2 is intended to remain traceable to the relational sequence established during Primary Calibration.Accordingly, the repository combines: Python implementations, structured JSON datasets, machine-readable exports, Markdown documentation, and supplementary appendices into one continuous and reproducible computational environment.These components represent different expressions of the same underlying relational architecture.K2 constitutes the computational foundation upon which the remaining verification architecture is built.Its outputs provide the operational basis for: K4 operational verification, K5 relational continuity, K6 secondary differentiation, and the subsequent summary and reference documentation contained elsewhere in the RP9 repository. K2. CODE & VALIDATION serves as the primary computational reproduction layer of the RP9 framework.It transforms the relational structure established during Primary Calibration into a complete operational environment through successive H-D-R development, structural expansion, CORE×4 generation, computational documentation, and reproducible validation.Rather than extending the theoretical framework, K2 demonstrates that the established relational architecture can be reproduced consistently through code, data, and documented computational procedures, thereby providing the operational foundation for the remainder of the Secondary Verification architecture.⚖️ License & CopyrightLicensed under RP9-LA-2026Copyright © 2026 Anton WallinSee LICENSE for the complete licensing terms

item.description: Generated: 2026-06-28T16:37:05 Script: RP9_CORE4_MANIFEST_POSITION_VALIDATOR.py Version: 1.0.0FINAL_PASS = True CLASSIFICATION = CORE4_MANIFEST_POSITION_IS_B5_WITH_B6_AS_INVERSE_LINE ANSWER = Core4's manifest initial position is the B5 line: normalized direction (1, 0, 1). B6 is the same observation line in inverted direction (-1, 0, -1). The position is thus operatorically generated from the H-D-R half-angle between X and Z, not chosen afterwards. When Vesica Piscis is defined as the XY front position and the H-D-R operator generates Core4, what position is manifested by the Core4 structure itself? Does this position coincide with B5-N6/B6-N6, or is a later observation selection required? The test examines the derived initial position, not the uniqueness of B5/B6 among already defined views. Start with Vesica Piscis in the XY plane looking straight ahead. Define X as the relational length and Z as the frontal observation normal. Derive the H-D-R half-angle between 0° and 90° in the XZ field without using B5/B6 as input. Read out the generated position. Check that the position is in Core4's own rotation/relation field. Then compare with the ABC definitions, including B5 and B6. X relation axis = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0] Z front normal = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] Manifest position = normalize(X + Z) = [0.707106781187, 0.0, 0.707106781187] Angle to X = 45.000000000000° Angle to Z = 45.000000000000° Y component zero = True 45/45 half-angle lock = True Directed position matches = ['B5'] Axis line matches = ['B5', 'B6'] Nearest ABC view = B5 Nearest ABC line angle = 0.0 Core4 contains manifest axis = True Core4's manifested starting position is the B5 line: normalized direction (1, 0, 1). B6 is the same observation line in the inverted direction (-1, 0, -1). The position is thus operatorically generated from the H-D-R half-angle between X and Z, not chosen a posteriori.B5 and B6 are opposite directions on the same observation line. With RP9's usual +X/+Z convention, the directed position becomes B5. B6 is the same line seen from the inverted direction. 01_JSON/CORE4_MANIFEST_POSITION_VALIDATION.json 02_CSV/ABC_POSITION_COMPARISON.csv 02_CSV/CORE4_AXIS_COMPARISON.csv 03_REPORT/CORE4_MANIFEST_POSITION_VALIDATION.md ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: CORE4. OPERATOR STATE DERIVATION VALIDATION
item.description: Generated: 2026-06-28T18:15:39 Script: RP9_CORE4_OPERATOR_STATE_DERIVATION_VALIDATOR.py Version: 1.0.0FINAL_PASS = True FINAL_ANSWER_CODE = B H0_STATUS = REJECTED H1_STATUS = ACCEPTED CLASSIFICATION = CORE4_OPERATOR_STATE_DERIVES_B5_WITH_B6_INVERSE_LINE STATEMENT = Core4 produces a unique operator-derived orientation before ABC comparison. After ABC comparison, the directed position coincides with B5 and the axis line with B5/B6. Is the Core4 observation orientation a necessary consequence of the H-D-R/Core4 structure, or does it only arise after a later observation selection through ABC/B5/B6? The validator tests the Core4 operator output orientation before ABC/B5/B6 is loaded. Core4 is generated from the rotation/circle structure. Relational center pair axes are extracted from the generated Core4 structure. The operator-state rule is applied without ABC/B5/B6: XZ half-angle, Y neutrality, positive relation to X and frontal Z. H0 tries to win through order change, inversions and rotational stress. ABC/B5/B6 is loaded only after the operator-state orientation has been derived. The derived orientation is compared to the ABC system. The test determines whether the B5/B6 position is a later observational choice or an orientation that already follows from the Core4 structure.operator_state_status = UNIQUE_OPERATOR_STATE_DERIVED passing_candidate_count = 2 unique_operator_line_count = 1 derived_vector = [0.707106781187, 0.0, 0.707106781187] directed_matches_after_abc = ['B5'] line_matches_after_abc = ['B5', 'B6'] What assumptions were made? Only the startframe is used: Vesica Piscis frontal position = XY, X = relational length, Z = frontal normal. ABC/B5/B6 are not used in the operator-state derivation. What data was used before ABC? The Core4 rotation list, generated circle centers and center pair axes. What data was not used before ABC? ABC classes, B5/B6 names, candidate uniqueness tables and previous manifest position inference were not used to derive the operator-state vector. Can the inference be reproduced without the ABC definitions? Yes for the operator-state vector. ABC is only required in the final comparison to name it as B5/B6 line. What was the falsification trying to do? It tried to support H0 by creating multiple equivalent operator-state orientations before ABC. H0 is only supported if an alternative survives the same rule. 01_JSON/CORE4_OPERATOR_STATE_DERIVATION_VALIDATION.json 02_CSV/CORE4_AXIS_CANDIDATES.csv 02_CSV/FALSIFICATION_CASES.csv 02_CSV/ABC_FINAL_COMPARISON.csv 03_REPORT/CORE4_OPERATOR_STATE_DERIVATION_VALIDATION.md 04_AUDIT/CORE4_OPERATOR_STATE_DERIVATION_AUDIT.json ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.

item.title: CORE4. INITIAL ORIENTATION VALIDATION
item.description: Generated: 2026-06-28T14:00:20 Script: RP9_CORE4_INITIAL_ORIENTATION_VALIDATOR.py Version: 1.0.0FINAL_PASS = True CLASSIFICATION = CORE4_GENERATES_B5B6_AXIS_BUT_NOT_UNIQUELY B5B6_AXIS_GENERATED_BY_CORE4 = True B5B6_AXIS_UNIQUE_AT_CORE4_INITIAL_STATE = False OTHER_XZ_DIAGONAL_GENERATED_BY_CORE4 = True When Core4 is generated from a frontal Vesica Piscis through H-D-R related rotation sequence, Core4 is already uniquely positioned according to B5/B6, or does B5/B6 arise first as the selected observation position? Core4 generates the B5/B6 axis from the beginning, but at the same time generates the second XZ diagonal. B5/B6 is therefore operatorically enabled/intrinsically present, but not uniquely fixed as a unique observation position before the observation lock.The test examines whether Core4's own generated relation axes already contain and uniquely fix the B5/B6 orientation before any A/B/C observation position is selected. Start with Vesica Piscis in the XY plane straight ahead. Generate 90° activation as a separate intermediate step. Generate Core4 through four ±45° relations according to the established Core4 sequence. Extract each relation's own centerline, elevation axis and normal axis. Compare the intrinsic axes against the B5/B6 axis without using B5/B6 as the generation input. Try to falsify uniqueness by searching for the second XZ diagonal. If B5/B6 is uniquely present as the only Core4 orientation before observation selection, the position is operatorically fixed. If B5/B6 is present but shares the field with an alternative diagonal, B5/B6 is operatorically generated but later observationally locked.Vesica Piscis frontal position: XY plane, normal Z ↓ H-D-R activation 1: 90° rotated 2D circles ↓ H-D-R activation 2: Core4, four relations / eight circles, ±45° ↓ Intrinsic axis readout before observation selection The falsification check finds the second XZ diagonal in the Core4 intrinsic relation field.This means that the B5/B6 axis is present from the beginning, but not as the only possible orientation axis in the Core4 initial state.This validator distinguishes between two different claims: The B5/B6 axis is operatorically generated in Core4. B5/B6 is uniquely fixed as the only observation position even before observation selection. The result confirms point 1.The result does not confirm point 2, since the second XZ diagonal is also generated in the Core4 initial state. 01_JSON/CORE4_INITIAL_ORIENTATION_VALIDATION.json 02_CSV/CORE4_AXIS_RECORDS.csv 03_REPORT/CORE4_INITIAL_ORIENTATION_VALIDATION.md ⚖️ — License & Copyright Licensed under RP9-LA-2026 Copyright © 2026 Anton Wallin See LICENSE for full terms.
